So, will the Big Ten make it four straight, or will a new conference emerge on top in 2026? The Buckeyes return quarterback Julian Sayin, who threw for 3,610 yards and 32 touchdowns as a freshman. He will once again have one of the best receivers in the country in Jeremiah Smith, who recorded 1,243 yards and 12 touchdowns last season after posting 1,315 yards (the most by a true freshman since 2000) and 15 touchdowns the year before. Meanwhile, Dante Moore will return for Oregon after completing 71.8% of his passes for 3,565 yards and 30 TDs last season. articles.title: Favorite underrated fantasy football draft picks from Rounds 1-11 in 10-team leagues
articles.summary: Playing in a 10-team fantasy football league? Here's a pick to consider in Rounds 1-11.
articles.body:
Everyone has their favorites, and I'm thrilled to share mine for the 2026 season. I've dissected Yahoo ADP and compared the results to my own projections to find the players who should have more value in our hosted leagues. This list is an even mix of safe options and high-ceiling players, with players selected from all positions and at all points in the draft.

With an ADP of Pick 9, Cook barely fits into the first round of 10-team leagues. But I'm drafting him over Jonathan Taylor, who is being selected three picks earlier, and I could make a case that he can be preferred over Christian McCaffrey, who has incredible upside but is also the riskiest first-round option.

The 2025 rushing champion is still in his prime at age 26 and has had a moderate career workload with 842 carries. Cook's membership in a Josh Allen-led offense gives him a much higher floor than Taylor, who is part of an unstable offensive unit and missed 16 games over the past four seasons.

I'm fully on board with the popular plan of starting with running backs in standard 2026 formats. Brown's heavy usage in an explosive Bengals passing game gives him a high floor. After all, the 26-year-old has tallied 123 catches and nine receiving scores over the past two seasons. Brown also has some rushing upside with 13 TDs over the past two seasons, as Joe Burrow is not a threat to steal many goal-line scores. Unless a manager is wary of Burrow's durability, Brown belongs in the same tier as Taylor and Cook.

I will happily select Bowers or Cardinals tight end Trey McBride in Round 3. Both players are good bets for 1,000-yard seasons, which will provide fantasy managers with a massive advantage over their opponents each week. My 2026 draft plan is to either go early or late at tight end, as most of the middle tier either have QB questions (Kyle Pitts Sr., Harold Fannin Jr.) or are returning from major injuries (Tucker Kraft, George Kittle).

There is a terrific tier of wide receivers in Round 4, with Flowers being my personal favorite ahead of Tee Higgins, Rashee Rice, Jaylen Waddle and Tetairoa McMillan. The Ravens are expected to throw the ball more often this season, which is good news for … wait … who are their other pass catchers?

Isaiah Likely left in free agency, Mark Andrews had 422 yards in 17 games last year, Ja'Kobi Lane is a rookie, Rashod Bateman has been a bust and Derrick Henry rarely catches passes. That leaves Flowers, who should improve on his 86-catch, 1,211-yard 2025 effort.

McConkey is the last receiver who requires little wish-casting to project a dominant season. After all, the third-year vet already enjoyed a terrific campaign when he caught 82 passes for 1,149 yards as a rookie in 2024. His role was limited last season in a Chargers offense that lacked creativity and battled OL injuries throughout the campaign. But the arrival of Mike McDaniel, who is so proficient at calling plays that he once made Tua Tagovailoa an NFL passing leader, is going to unleash the Chargers offense, with McConkey being the primary beneficiary.

I'm not worried about age when it comes to Adams, as Hall of Fame receivers of his ilk often age well. Adams, who scored 14 TDs in 14 games last season, will continue to be part of a prolific Rams passing attack that has a surprisingly narrow range of options for Matthew Stafford. After all, Sean McVay offenses rarely throw to running backs, and the Rams lack an established third receiver. The tight ends will combine for a solid reception total, but there will be plenty of passes directed in Adams' direction.

I'll throw this thought out there: what if we haven't seen the best of the ultra-talented Williams? The former Alabama star projected as a No. 1 receiver when the Lions selected him 12th overall in 2022, only to see injuries, a lack of maturity and inattention to detail slow his progress.

Williams has made strides each season, and Jared Goff recently raved about his training camp improvements . The Lions have a favorable schedule and an offensive coordinator (Drew Petzing) who loves to throw the ball. Williams is already one of football's best deep threats and could be a fantasy star if he can catch a couple more underneath passes each game.

The middle rounds are meant for chasing upside, which is the case for Williams in Round 7 and Washington in Round 8. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen is known for creating fantasy stars, and his next one may be Washington, who played at a 1,200-yard pace over his final nine games of 2025. Brian Thomas Jr. will run deep patterns as the X receiver and Jakobi Meyers will catch a few balls each week, but Washington is the man who will lead the team in targets.

This group is full of defenses and uninspiring options. Instead, I'll grab two players from the next two rounds.

I'm waiting on QB this year, as the position is incredibly flat and deep. Nix and Brock Purdy are fine options in Round 10. I'll choose Nix, who quietly led the NFL in passing attempts last season and was handed a No. 1 receiver when the team acquired Jaylen Waddle. Nix also has a solid rushing floor, having averaged 393 yards in his two seasons. And with Waddle by his side, he figures to establish a new career-high in passing yards and TDs.

Round 11: Kyler Murray, QB, Vikings (or Jared Goff, QB, Lions)

Truthfully, I like Murray and Goff as much as Nix and Purdy for those who have the conviction to wait on drafting a QB. Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell is an elite offensive guru, who can only be stopped by the horrific QB play of J.J. McCarthy. With O'Connell running the show and Justin Jefferson attacking the secondary, Murray is in a much better situation than any of his years with Arizona. And of course, Murray has a rushing ceiling that can be matched by only a few QBs.

That said, I wouldn't argue with anyone who prefers Goff and his ultra-high floor as the leader of one of football's best offenses. After all, Goff has averaged 4,552 yards and 32.5 passing TDs over the past four seasons, and the Lions offense shows no signs of slowing down.

articles.title: Examining key rookies from the 2026 class and what role they'll play in fantasy football to start this season
articles.summary: What can you expect from some of the top rookies in fantasy football to start the 2026 season?
articles.body:
The preseason is over, fantasy football drafts are hitting their peak and we finally have a clearer picture of which rookies can actually help us in Year 1. There are only a couple I feel comfortable calling weekly starters right now, but this class has plenty of flex options, upside stashes and players who could become very valuable as the season unfolds.

Yes, Love is dealing with a high-ankle sprain, but once that ankle is cleared and he's ready to go, you're starting him every single week. His preseason debut was just a glimpse of the type of production we could get from a true three-down running back who can beat defenses on the ground and through the air. Love has weekly RB2 value with legitimate RB1 upside once healthy, although Arizona was still working him back from the injury entering the final week of August.

Seattle kept Price under wraps for basically the entire preseason, and I don't view that as a negative at all. They wanted their first-round running back healthy for Week 1 because he's going to command a significant workload in this offense. There may be questions about how much receiving work he gets, but the rushing volume and scoring opportunity should make Price a weekly starter right out of the gate.

Tate finished the entire preseason without a catch, and some of the excitement surrounding him earlier this summer has understandably cooled off. I'm not stressing over the talent or the opportunity because he's still going to be one of Cam Ward's primary targets, and he finished Titans training camp with seven catches and two touchdowns in a joint practice against Chicago. This might be a slower burn in a Tennessee offense that I don't project to be great, but Tate remains firmly on the flex radar.

Cleveland is going to find ways to get Concepcion the football. We've already seen him used through the air, on the ground and in the return game, and the explosiveness jumps off the screen. The bigger concern for me is Cleveland's offense and quarterback situation, but the talent and designed touches give Concepcion immediate flex appeal.

Stribling has looked great throughout the preseason, and you should be drafting him with the intention of potentially playing him early. There are still questions surrounding the health of San Francisco's veteran pass-catchers, including George Kittle and Mike Evans, which could open an even larger opportunity for the rookie. He's a flex-worthy receiver already, with the potential for significantly more depending on how this 49ers depth chart looks entering the season.

Boston didn't give us much statistically during the preseason, but Cleveland didn't need to see much from him because he earned first-team work throughout camp. He's a big outside receiver with the type of frame that could make him an immediate factor around the end zone. There are a lot of mouths to feed in Cleveland, but at his price, Boston is an intriguing deep-league flex option with upside.

Tyson is the definition of stash and wait. He suffered a significant hamstring injury after already missing valuable offseason time, and the Saints placed him on injured reserve to start the season, meaning he'll miss at least the first four games. He was injured in the middle of August and given an initial timeline of two months for a return. You're not drafting Tyson expecting to play him anytime soon, but if you've got an IR spot, the talent and eventual opportunity make him worth holding.

Lemon missed most of camp with a hamstring injury, then his preseason debut definitely wasn't the type of performance anybody wanted to see. I'm still not giving up on the talent, but I don't expect him to immediately be a full-time player in two-receiver sets. This feels like a much slower burn where we check back around the middle of the season and see what his role has become.

Coleman currently projects as the third running back in Denver behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey, so there's not much we can do with him early. But we've played this game with Dobbins long enough to know the health questions aren't going anywhere. Coleman is exactly the type of running back I want sitting at the end of my bench because it feels more like a matter of when an opportunity opens than if.

Washington is a stash, but he's a stash I absolutely do not want getting past me late in drafts. He was outstanding throughout the preseason, rushing for 168 yards on 23 carries, and Ashton Jeanty's ankle injury has created some uncertainty heading into the season. Washington can go from a bench stash to a weekly fantasy starter very quickly if Jeanty misses time.

Johnson looked like Kansas City's second-best running back during the preseason, and I loved what we saw from him both as a runner and receiver. There's probably not enough opportunity to matter while Kenneth Walker III is healthy and commanding the backfield. But if something happens to Walker, Johnson becomes a much more interesting player in an offense we expect to score plenty of points.

It was a pretty quiet preseason for Cooper, which isn't exactly what fantasy managers wanted to see from a first-round pick. I'm still interested because Geno Smith gives this Jets passing game a chance to be significantly better, and there should eventually be opportunity for Cooper to carve out a role. In normal redraft leagues, though, I'd rather monitor him and potentially grab him off waivers once we actually see the routes and targets increase.

Betting on rookie tight ends is already difficult enough before we start adding missed practices and injuries into the equation. Sadiq lost valuable time throughout the offseason and currently sits behind Mason Taylor, so I'm not spending meaningful draft capital here. In normal one-tight end leagues, leave him on waivers and make him prove that the role is there first.

Singleton finished the preseason with another 44 scrimmage yards against Chicago, but he's still buried behind Tony Pollard and Tyjae Spears. I'm not ready to call him Tennessee's future at the position, and I'm definitely not expecting meaningful touches early. He's a deep stash whose value changes quickly if Spears, who has dealt with durability issues, misses time.

Don't draft Mendoza in standard one-QB leagues. Kirk Cousins appears positioned to open the season ahead of him, even though Las Vegas has not officially announced its Week 1 starter as of Monday morning. Quarterback is too deep to burn a bench spot waiting on a rookie who may not play, so if Mendoza gets his opportunity later in the season, you can deal with it on waivers then.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton sold his entire car collection, only to find his dream Ferrari F40 after 30 years in a dusty garage: here’s the incredible story
articles.summary: International Sports News: The seven-time Formula 1 world champion has revealed his “very own F40,” and the Ferrari isn't just another addition to a celebrity garage. Hamilton s.
articles.body: The seven-time Formula 1 world champion has revealed his “very own F40,” and the Ferrari isn't just another addition to a celebrity garage. Hamilton says it is the car of his dreams, something he has wanted since he was a kid. And somehow, the story of how he found it makes the whole thing even better.Lewis Hamilton had sold his entire car collection, then a dusty Ferrari F40 changed everythingHamilton shared a series of photos on Instagram showing the iconic Ferrari F40 in various stages of restoration, from its dusty, neglected state to its time inside Ferrari's facilities at Maranello. The car had reportedly been sitting in a garage for more than 30 years, according to Hamilton himself.“My very own F40. This is the car of my dreams and has been for as long as I can remember.”That line pretty much tells you everything.Hamilton said he dreamed of owning an F40 as a kid. So when he joined Ferrari in 2025, he made sure one was waiting for him on his first day at Maranello because, as he put it, “that’s how much it means to me.”And this is where the story gets interesting.The Ferrari Hamilton eventually found wasn't sitting pretty in a showroom. It had been left in a garage for over three decades, covered in dust. Hamilton said that once he found it, he knew he had to bring it home.Then came Maranello.Hamilton sent the F40 to Ferrari's factory, where the company's engineers and mechanics spent weeks working on the car and bringing it back to life. His photos show the Ferrari stripped down during the restoration process, with the mechanical work clearly underway before the finished car emerged looking like the machine Hamilton had dreamed about for years.And there's an even bigger twist to this story.Just last year, Hamilton revealed that he had sold his entire car collection.At the 2025 Azerbaijan Grand Prix, he said he no longer owned any of his road cars and had shifted his attention toward art. His former collection included some seriously rare machinery, including a Pagani Zonda 760LH, Ferrari LaFerrari and Mercedes-AMG Project One. But when he was asked whether there was one car that could tempt him back into ownership, Hamilton didn't hesitate.The legendary Ferrari F40“If I was going to get a car, it would be the F40,” he said at the time, describing it more like a piece of art than just another car.Fast-forward less than a year, and Hamilton has done exactly that.The timing makes the reveal feel almost scripted. He went from “I don't have any cars anymore” to owning the one Ferrari he had openly admitted he still dreamed about.And for Hamilton, the F40 isn't difficult to understand.The legendary Ferrari was introduced in 1987 as the company's 40th-anniversary supercar and has become one of the most coveted cars ever to wear the Prancing Horse badge. But for Hamilton, its value seems to go beyond the price tag or rarity.This was the car he wanted before he became a seven-time world champion, before Ferrari, before the millions and before the massive garage full of supercars.Now, after more than 30 years sitting under dust, his childhood dream is finally back where it belongs, in his hands.And Hamilton isn't finished teasing the story. “I can’t wait to share more with you all. Stay tuned…” he wrote.So, yes, there may be more to this F40 story coming. And considering where this one started, abandoned in a garage for three decades, we're definitely paying attentionGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Former Toronto Maple Leafs forward Calle Jarnkrok is leaving the NHL and returning to Sweden after signing a three-year contract with Brynas IF of the Swedish Hockey League (SHL). This will end his four year contract with the Toronto. Earlier, the player signed an $8.4 million contract with the Toronto Maple Leafs in 2022, which carried an average annual value of $2.1 million. According to reports, his most successful NHL season came during his first year with the Maple Leafs in 2022-23. The 34-year-old scored 20 goals on the campaign and grabbed 39 total points.Calle Jarnkrok departs the NHL after his $8.4 million deal ends and returns to Sweden to play in the Swedish Hockey LeagueFormer Toronto Maple Leafs forward Calle Jarnkrok has decided to depart from the NHL, and the forward is reportedly planning to join the Swedish Hockey League. Reports suggest that he has already signed a three-year contract with Brynas IF of the Swedish Hockey League.His most successful NHL season came during his first year with the Maple Leafs in 2022-23. The Swedish player scored 20 goals on the campaign and grabbed 39 total points. In the NHL, he has recorded 75 points in 200 games with the club. Earlier, he has played with multiple teams such as the Nashville Predators, Seattle Kraken, and Calgary Flames.In fact, The Athletic's Chris Johnston had previously ranked him 72nd among this summer's unrestricted free agents and suggested that the veteran forward could be looking for a change of scenery after a difficult season.After his contract expired, the Swedish player decided that instead of signing another NHL contract, he opted to return to the club where his professional career began.He expressed excitement about rejoining Brynäs and being back in front of the team's supporters. “I am very happy to be back in Brynäs IF, and it feels fantastic that it is now complete,” Järnkrok said. The forward further added he is looking forward to meeting his new teammates and playing in front of the Brynäs fans again.Meanwhile, Maple Leafs general manager John Chayka has added forwards like Jack Roslovic, Teddy Blueger, Colton Sissons, and Brandon Duhaime. He also traded for veteran Nick Paul and selected Gavin McKenna with the first overall draft pick. According to Daily Faceoff’s projections, Paul, Sissons, and Duhaime are expected to be the new Toronto Maple Leafs fourth line.Järnkrok leaves Toronto with more than $22 million in NHL career earnings and a reputation as a versatile two-way forward capable of playing both center and wing and contributing on special teams. articles.title: When did Novak Djokovic marry wife Jelena? All about their wedding and love story
articles.summary: International Sports News: Novak Djokovic married his longtime girlfriend Jelena Ristic on July 10, 2014, in Montenegro, just four days after winning his second Wimbledon title..
articles.body: Novak Djokovic married his longtime girlfriend Jelena Ristic on July 10, 2014, in Montenegro, just four days after winning his second Wimbledon title. The couple held their civil wedding at the Aman Sveti Stefan resort on the Adriatic coast, while a private church ceremony followed on July 12. Jelena was pregnant with their first child at the time. The wedding came after years of a relationship that began when the two met as teenagers in Belgrade and later stayed together despite long periods apart. Their son Stefan was born three months later, followed by daughter Tara in 2017.Novak Djokovic and Jelena Djokovic married days after his Wimbledon winThe timing made July 2014 especially memorable for Novak Djokovic. On July 6, he defeated Roger Federer in a five-set Wimbledon final and lifted his second title at the tournament. During his celebration, Djokovic dedicated the win to his future wife and their unborn child.“I would like to dedicate it to my future wife and our future baby,” Djokovic said after the victory. “I’m going to become a father soon and I’m still preparing for that. It’s a great joy in life.”Four days later, he and Jelena exchanged vows at Aman Sveti Stefan in Montenegro. The civil ceremony was followed by a church wedding on July 12 at the Church of Saint Stephen, with the second ceremony kept private for close family.Jelena wore an ivory wedding dress designed by Sarah Burton for Alexander McQueen. Djokovic later spoke about seeing her for the first time as his bride, describing the moment in emotional terms.“Seeing her for the first time in her wedding dress, smiling and walking towards me… She looked like an angel,” Djokovic told Hello! magazine. “I was focused on her, and her smile and our baby. It really was a perfect moment.”The wedding came as the couple prepared for a major change in their lives. Their son Stefan was born in October 2014, only a few months after they became husband and wife.Novak Djokovic and Jelena Djokovic’s relationship began in high schoolThe story of Novak Djokovic and Jelena Djokovic goes back much further than their wedding day. They first met during their high school years in Belgrade and began their relationship in 2005.Their early years were not always easy. Jelena studied at Bocconi University in Milan while Djokovic was building his tennis career, leaving them to manage a long-distance relationship. Jelena later explained how difficult travel was for them when they were younger.“I was a student barely getting by, and he was a very young tennis player who also had no money to spare on expensive trips,” she has explained. “Airplanes were, at the time, something utterly out of our reach. We contrived and devised these plans how to meet, how to make our relationship work.”Djokovic proposed to Jelena in September 2013, after the couple had spent years together. Their engagement was publicly confirmed that month, with Djokovic sharing his happiness about calling Jelena his future wife.By the time they married, their relationship had already lasted for nearly a decade. Djokovic later told People, “She’s the only serious relationship I ever had. She’s been my girlfriend, fiancée and my wife for more than 20 years, and I’m eternally grateful for her love, her support, the relationship that has evolved over the years.”Jelena has also remained closely involved in the Novak Djokovic Foundation, where she serves as global CEO. The foundation focuses on early childhood education and preschool development in Serbia. The couple have since raised two children, Stefan and Tara, while Jelena has continued to support Novak both personally and through their shared work.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ex-Giants Starter Claimed off Waivers by New England Patriots
articles.summary: Former New York Giants starting linebacker claimed off waivers by New England Patriots. The post Ex-Giants Starter Claimed off Waivers by New England Patriot...
articles.body:
One former New York Giants starter has found a new home with a Super Bowl contender.

"Patriots claimed LB Darius Muasau from the Giants," ESPN's Adam Schefter wrote on his official X account on Monday.

"Darius Muasau was a core special teamer for the Giants in 2024, but scaled back to mainly kick return and punt coverage teams after climbing the depth chart last season," Patriots reporter Taylor Kyles wrote on his official X account on Monday. "Muasau returned to a primary ST role this preseason and had multiple standout reps, including 3 total tackles."

Muasau was the only player cut by the Giants claimed off waivers by another team — conversely, the Giants were not awarded any players off waivers.

"The Patriots have claimed LB Darius Muasau and TE Cameron Latu off waivers," Patriots reporter Carlos A. Lopez wrote on his official X account on Monday. "Muasau, 25, was a sixth-round pick by the Giants in 2024 and has started 18 games over the last two seasons, recording 100+ tackles, 1 sack, and 1 interception. Latu, 26, is a former third-round pick out of Alabama who spent last season with the Eagles, appearing in 15 games."

Darius Muasau Gets Real Chance With Pats

Muasau will now get a chance to do something he was never going to get to do again for the Giants — actually get on the field.

The Patriots, the defending AFC Champions, have a concrete need for depth at inside linebacker and will likely have a big role for Muasau on special teams.

"Patriots found a new No. 3 LB with Darius Muasau," Patriots reporter Mark Daniels wrote on his official X account.

Giants Opened & Closed 2026 Draft With Linebackers

Muasau probably realized the clock was ticking when the Giants used their 1st and last picks in the 2026 NFL Draft on players at his position.

The Giants took what seems like a generational talent in the 1st round with Ohio State linebacker Arvell Reese , a 6-foot-4, 243-pound playmaking machine. They closed things out with their final pick in the 6th round by taking BYU inside linebacker Jack Kelly .

"The Giants see Kelly as a versatile player who can play off-ball linebacker and edge," ESPN's Jordan Raanan wrote in April . "Scouts Inc. called him a 'thickly built linebacker' who had 10 sacks this past season at BYU. The Giants also see special teams value in Kelly's game, which is where he could make an immediate impact. Kelly was the seventh and final pick of Harbaugh's first draft class with the Giants, which fit the mold of what he's been trying to accomplish — becoming bigger and more physical."

ENDWELL, N.Y. (WIVT/WBGH) - One former Maine-Endwell Spartans football star who helped lead the team to a state championship as offensive MVP in 2022 officially opened his season and collegiate career with St. Thomas.

Anthony Policare, who made the move over from Buffalo to the Tommies this past offseason, would start for the team as they opened their season against Division II Winona State. In the team's 15-9 win at home, he would throw 13-for-22 for 166 yards and a touchdown in the game, while also rushing for 73 yards and getting in the end zone using his legs as well.

It is reported that he is in a QB1 battle, so he did well to show out in his debut.

We'll see if he keeps his spot when he heads on the road with the Tommies on Saturday to face North Dakota.

articles.title: Former Tennessee football assistant coach, Sweetwater star Kippy Brown dies at 71
articles.summary: Former Tennessee football assistant coach Kippy Brown died Aug. 31 at 71. Brown won a Super Bowl as an assistant coach with the Seattle Seahawks in 2014.
articles.body:
Former Tennessee football assistant coach Charles "Kippy" Brown has died. He was 71.

Brown was a trailblazer as the first Black quarterback to play at Sweetwater High School in 1969, and he led the Wildcats to back-to-back state championships in 1971 and 1972. Brown was recruited by Tennessee in high school, but opted to go play for Memphis. He became the first Black quarterback to play for Memphis, which was known as Memphis State when he played from 1974-77.

Brown eventually worked under three different Vols football coaches before winning Super Bowl XLVIII with the Seattle Seahawks in 2014. The Seahawks notched a 43-8 victory over the Peyton Manning-led Denver Broncos.

Brown was the wide receivers coach at Tennessee under Johnny Majors from 1983-89 and then again for Phillip Fulmer from 1993-94 as assistant head coach. Tennessee acquired the nickname "Wide Receiver U" when Brown worked for Majors, as Brown coached receivers like Anthony Miller, Tim McGee, Alvin Harper and Carl Pickens to greatness.

Fulmer said having Brown on his staff was a "fantastic time in our life," in a 2015 documentary produced by The Bingham Group.

"Kippy is smart, he's energetic, his personality is infectious. He's a great recruiter, and he's a detailed football coach," Fulmer said. "It really came together at a great time for us in our careers. We kind of changed the culture at Tennessee back to a winning program. We just had a lot of fun doing it."

Brown returned to Knoxville again in 2009 when Lane Kiffin hired him as wide receivers coach and passing game coordinator before the Chick-fil-A Bowl in December of 2009. Less than a month later, Brown was named the interim head coach after Kiffin left Tennessee for Southern Cal after one season.

UT instead hired Derek Dooley to replace Kiffin. Brown returned to the NFL as the wide receivers coach for Pete Carroll from 2010-14, and the Seahawks went to two straight Super Bowls before Brown retired in 2015.

articles.title: Vikings Officially Announce 15 Practice Squad Signings
articles.summary: Plenty of familiar faces on the list
articles.body:
While there were not a lot of individual announcements for us to track , the Minnesota Vikings were signing players to the practice squad on Monday, coming to terms with fifteen players, almost all of whom were with the team during training camp.

Here is the full list of players the team has brought back.

There had been a report from NFL reporter Aaron Wilson that the Vikings had signed former Cincinnati Bengals tight end Cam Grandy to the practice squad as well. Whether that report was inaccurate (which would be odd) or the deal simply was not worked out prior to the NFL's transaction deadline, Grandy's name was not on the list of practice squad signings that the team released.

Of the fifteen players the team signed to the practice squad, fourteen of them went through training camp with the Vikings this season. The lone exception is Nelson, who was a seventh-round pick of the Atlanta Falcons in the 2025 NFL Draft out of Wisconsin. He appeared in 10 games for the Falcons last year, almost exclusively on special teams. According to Pro Football Reference , he played only four snaps on offense.

The Vikings might be interested in bringing back either quarterback Max Brosmer or wide receiver Dillon Bell to the practice squad, as both of those players were waived on Monday to make room for the team's two waiver claims , Nick Samac and Trevor Keegan. If that's the case, both of those players will have to be on waivers for 24 hours (and go unclaimed, of course) in order for the Vikings to bring them back to the practice squad.

But, as it stands for now, that is your Minnesota Vikings practice squad, folks. What do you think about the players the Vikings brought back?

articles.title: MLB Insider Praises Cardinals for Stunning Turnaround amid Rebuild
articles.summary: The St. Louis Cardinals have been a much better team than expected in 2026. After trading Brendan Donovan, Sonny Gray, Nolan Arenado and Willson Contreras, t...
articles.body:
The St. Louis Cardinals have been a much better team than expected in 2026. After trading Brendan Donovan, Sonny Gray, Nolan Arenado and Willson Contreras, the Cardinals were picked by many to finish at the bottom of the National League Central, much like they did in 2023.

However, while they are essentially out of postseason contention, they are only two games below .500 entering the final month of the season, and there have actually been quite a few success stories, including the emergence of Jordan Walker, which included him winning the Home Run Derby.

Other players such as JJ Wetherholt, Joshua Baez, Ivan Herrera, Riley O'Brien and Alec Burleson have also emerged as mainstays of the team's core. The Cardinals have taken several steps forward this year despite what their 68-70 record would indicate.

Katie Woo of The Athletic discussed the Cardinals' transformation under first-year president of baseball operations Chaim Bloom, and had a lot of positive things to say.

"Looking at the Cardinals now, we have so many more answers about this club, the players in it and their future direction just from this season alone than we have in the last probably three years combined," Woo said on the "Dealin' the Cards" podcast.

"When you add that on top of a record that all things considered is not terrible given what we were expecting at the start of the year, that is the most encouraging sign. I would encourage fans to be a little bit more open minded in this specific situation because for so long, the big thing with the Cardinals is what's their plan. They've made a ton of changes and we've seen their plan, and we've already seen some early returns on the answers.

"That I think has made this season, regardless of how they finish in the win-loss record a success."

Katie Woo Praises St. Louis Cardinals Changes Amid Shocking Turnaround

Chaim Bloom has worked tirelessly to ensure that the Cardinals make the necessary changes and become a consistent contender again. Now, there is a light at the end of the tunnel for St. Louis, and their window to return to contention is becoming clearer.

While some of their star players are surely missed by fans, the fanbase also understands that it's going to take a little time before the Cardinals are back in the postseason again. Given how low expectations were entering the 2026 season, they have done surprisingly well since Bloom took over for John Mozeliak.

Why St. Louis Cardinals Could Be Contenders Again Soon

The Cardinals are still likely a few years away from being a contender, but they have taken a lot of important steps forward this season. Walker has become the player the Cardinals always thought they had, and Wetherholt has remained in the race for the NL Rookie of the Year award along with Sal Stewart.

They still need some pitching if they want to get back in the race as soon as 2027 or 2028, and just a few additions won't make them a World Series contender, but the future is bright in St. Louis for a change.

articles.title: Bill Guerin speaks out about Quinn Hughes’ extension
articles.summary: Minnesota Wild General Manager Bill Guerin was at the Minnesota State Fair on Monday. He shared more information about extending star defenseman Quinn Hughes...
articles.body:
Minnesota Wild General Manager Bill Guerin was at the Minnesota State Fair on Monday. He shared more information about extending star defenseman Quinn Hughes.

Guerin sat on the Chad Hartman Show and was asked about the latest on re-signing Hughes. Furthermore, the relationship between Hughes and Guerin is in a good place. The two sides are still trying to hammer out the best deal possible.

This time last year, Guerin and the Wild were in the middle of trying to extend forward Kirill Kaprizov.

Except Guerin said trying to extend Hughes has a different feel to it than it did when they re-signed Kaprizov. Kaprizov signed an 8-year $136 million deal last September.

"The relationship is good between me and Quinn and his agent," Guerin told Hartman. "There's no tension. Communication has been good. I don't have anything disheartening to say."

Hughes' camp and the Wild have chatted about a new deal in-person twice this summer. Guerin said this in his interview at the state fair.

As the negotiation continues, Guerin is aware that when higher-profile players such as Hughes require a new contract, there is a lot of thought that goes into it.

Hughes was traded from the Vancouver Canucks last season after deciding that it was in his best interest to move on. Now, the Canucks have kick-started a rebuild, and Hughes is closer to chasing a Stanley Cup in Minnesota.

"They're figuring out what they want to do in their career and their life. It's pretty heavy," Guerin said of NHL superstars deciding on long-term deals.

So, are Guerin and the Wild convinced that Hughes sees himself in Minnesota for the foreseeable future?

"No good comes from answering a question like that," Guerin told Hartman.

If Hughes doesn't see a long-term future he's happy with in Minnesota, then the next question gets asked. What would the Wild get in return for him in a trade to a destination of his liking?

"Business is business. I can't say what I would or wouldn't do. This game is a business, and you conduct yourself in a businesslike manner. That's both sides," Guerin said. "I don't like getting into hypotheticals."

Influence of Makar's deal on Hughes' future

When the Colorado Avalanche officially signed defenseman Cale Makar to his record-breaking 8-year, $163.2 million contract, that did not change the tenor of how Guerin was negotiating. He continued talks with Hughes' camp.

The financial implication for Minnesota is clear: Makar becomes the first player to be paid north of $20 million every season under his new contract. Hughes may not be too far behind when he signs his next deal.

However, in this case, the Wild don't seem to be willing to roll over and pay Hughes the same right off the bat. To Guerin, Makar's case is completely separate, and he wants to keep it that way.

"There's a bar with Cale Makar signing that contract in Colorado, but Quinn might be after different things," Guerin said. "He's a different guy. He has a different personality and has different things in his life that are important to him. Who knows what he's really going to want in the end."

Since no extension has been signed, Hughes has been mulling over the best decision for his career. Moreover, there has been speculation that Quinn would like to play with his brother Jack and Luke, who are on the New Jersey Devils .

When the Canucks traded Quinn, he was already on the road and visiting with his brothers. When the deal was made for him to go to Minnesota, Guerin flew over to pick him up.

Jack said it was a "letdown" that he didn't see his brother moved to the Devils, but that ought to be water under the bridge now.

Well, it's not since Quinn is due to make this life-altering choice sooner rather than later. One that leaves fans pondering if that's a path he's seriously considering.

While it remains speculation at this time, Quinn going to play with his brothers still seems like it could be on the table.

articles.summary: Welcome to Bleacher Report's live coverage of WWE Raw on August 31. Keep it locked right here for live updates throughout the show.
articles.body:
Welcome to Bleacher Report's live coverage of WWE Raw on August 31. Keep it locked right here for live updates throughout the show.

When WWE heads to Mexico City, Penta will challenge Reigns for the world title. The OTC came out to the ring as Penta was celebrating.

Fenix hit a corkscrew to take Penta down at ringside. He hit a cutter, but Penta had to make it work because Fenix was about to miss.

Both men hit a couple of nice kicks to take each other down at the same time. Neither man could keep the upper hand for long, so the match was very competitive.

Penta popped Fenix into the air for a really cool powerbomb, but it only got him a two-count. He tried a hurricanrana, but Fenix flipped and landed on his feet.

He almost hit Penta with the Mexican Muscle Buster, but it got countered with a Penta Driver for a near-fall. They went out of the ring, and he hit another Penta Driver on the announce table.

When they got back into the ring, Fenix hit a nice hurricanrana for a two-count before Penta hit the Mexican Destroyer for the win.

The main event was the finals in the tournament to find a No. 1 contender for the world title. Penta and Fenix made their way to the ring for their first singles match in WWE as opponents.

The Lucha Bros shook hands before locking up and trading chest chops. They immediately turned it into a fast-paced exchange of takedowns and counters, but they came to a stalemate.

Fenix hit a couple of hurricanranas, but Penta countered a handspring with a dropkick before hitting a dive over the top rope.

Becky Lynch and Stephanie Vaquer had a confrontation backstage where they disagreed about whether Vaquer owes her anything.

Fenix was shown preparing for his match against his brother in the locker room.

Mysterio and McDonagh vs. Evans and Hendry Part 3

Mysterio made a blind tag so he could surprise Evans from behind with an attack. The Young OG spent a little time on defense while Judgment Day kept him cornered with double-team attacks.

Evans hit a move similar to Whisper in the Wind before making the hot tag to a fresh Hendry. He hit both opponents with a fallaway slam at the same time.

After McDonagh helped get control back, Mysterio ended up hitting Hendry with a frog splash for the win.

Mysterio and McDonagh vs. Hendry and Evans Part 2

Dirty Dom maintained control with some help from McDonagh's interference. He started taunting Evans and talking trash, which fired the young man up.

When the fight spilled out of the ring, Je'Von tried to get a running start around the ring, but McDonagh nailed him with a clothesline to cause a disqualification.

Joe Hendry ran down to make the save for Evans and take out both members of Judgment Day. Adam Pearce came out and restarted it as a tag team match.

Hendry and Evans easily took control, and Je'Von was able to run a lap around the ring before hitting a big dive.

Dominik Mysterio vs. Je'Von Evans Part 1

The next matchup saw Dominik Mysterio take on Je'Von Evans. As usual, JD McDonagh was with Dirty Dom for support.

Dom attacked Evans before he could get in the ring to get an early advantage. Evans told the ref he was good to go, so the bell rang and they got going. The Young OG immediately hit a few high-flying moves to take the AAA champion down.

McDonagh distracted Evans so Mysterio could hit a sneak attack. As we went to a break, Evans hit a big dive over the top rope.

Reigns said being the Tribal Chief is a burden because everyone wants what he has. He said instead of celebrating Penta and Fenix for making it to the finals of the tournament, he has to deal with other issues like Solo Sikoa.

He said he is going to make Solo acknowledge him and serve the family legacy, and he questions why he turned on the family to side with LA Knight. This brought out Knight to respond.

Sikoa was shown after having been attacked backstage, and Knight ran to the back to check on him. Once again, the blood was censored. Reigns attacked Knight when he got backstage.

Roman Reigns arrived backstage and told Fatu to handle his business with Keys because he has other things to deal with. He went to the ring for the next segment.

Page used the apron to trip Lee and regain control. He hit a nice suplex, but he still couldn't get the pin.

The Dragon hit a series of strikes as he started building up a head of steam. He jumped over the top rope and hit a nice hurricanrana to send Page into the announce table, but when he went for a second dive, Page countered.

All Ego sent Lee into Gable, who was sitting next to the commentators. Page tried to use an exposed turnbuckle to his advantage, but Gable snitched to the ref. The momentary distraction allowed Lee to hit Operation Dragon for the win.

All Ego used his size advantage to take control with a shoulder block. He caught Lee during a jump and slammed him to the mat before going after his neck.

Page had the upper hand for a couple of minutes, but one quick sequence in the corner put Lee in the driver's seat. He nailed a running dropkick in the corner for a quick two-count.

Gable talked about his history with luchadores and his journey to becoming the IC champion. He thanked the Mexican people for helping him see the way.

He said there are a lot of people deserving of a title opportunity before inviting Dragon Lee to the ring. Before long, Ethan Page came out and said it should be him who gets the title shot.

Gable said he was on the list of people who deserve a shot, but Lee took exception to being interrupted. Gable suggested they fight for a title shot right now.

WWE aired a video to hype Penta vs. Fenix for later in the show. It did a nice job highlighting their career together, even though they couldn't use any AEW footage.

Up next, Chad Gable came out for a promo.

Since the show was pre-taped, the Netflix feed cut away to a non-existent commercial break before coming back right away.

Sol hit a few nice moves that led to a missile dropkick. She ended up hitting a sunset flip powerbomb to take Raquel off the apron to the floor. Roxanne Perez and Liv Morgan ran to the ring, but Ruca took them out before they could do anything.

Lyra Valkyria ended up interfering and preventing the Sol Snatcher, which allowed Rodriguez to hit her finisher for the win.

Sol Ruca vs. Raquel Rodriguez (IC Title) Part 1

Ruca took on Raquel Rodriguez for the women's intercontinental title in the first bout. Before the match could get started, Jacob Fatu interrupted and got on the announce table to call out OTM and Keys. His mic was cut off after he started swearing.

When the bell rang, Raquel hit a clothesline to take control right away. She cornered the former champion for a series of back elbows.

Ruca used her speed and agility to knock Rodriguez out of the ring and hit a beautiful moonsault over the top rope to the floor. Rodriguez regained the upper hand for a moment, but Ruca kept herself in the fight.

Jey Uso was apparently busted open because his face was blurred out while people were checking on them. Back in the arena, Sol Ruca came out for the first match.

Raw opened with a shot backstage of OTM and Royce Keys attacking The Usos backstage.

articles.title: Ismael Saibari explains the dual nature of Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany
articles.summary: Do players turned coaches find it easier to win locker rooms?
articles.body:
Bayern Munich's coach is known for his affectionate personality and for being loved by his squad. However, Kompany is also a demanding manager who does not shy away from confrontation and is willing to push his players to their limits. Club newcomer Ismael Saibari explained this dichotomy in his gaffer.

In a recent interview with Bundesliga , the 25-year-old was asked about Kompany's style of coaching. "He's a really nice guy. During games, he becomes very passionate. But I think that's normal. Every footballer, when they go onto the pitch, is more passionate. Sometimes they do stupid stuff just because of the emotions. But I don't mind that," answered Saibari.

Successfully handling the locker room has been one of the biggest strengths for Kompany's success with Bayern. The winning culture established at the club synced superbly with the Belgian coach's unrelenting drive for improvement. In his second season numerous records were smashed by his team as they lifted the elusive DFB-Pokal after a six-year wait. Apart from the results, the brand of football Bayern play has won the hearts of fans, management and neutral watchers alike.

articles.title: Miami Hurricanes Football Week 1 Coaches Press Conference Recap
articles.summary: Cristobal, Dawson, and Hetherman take the podium to discuss Week 1 and Stanford
articles.body:
For the first time in the 2026 season, IT'S GAME WEEK!!!

Monday (8/31) was the weekly coaches press conference. Miami Head Coach Mario Cristobal, Offensive Coordinator Shannon Dawson, and Defensive Coordinator Corey Hethermen took the podium for the first time this season.

Head Coach Mario Cristobal: "We had a chance to watch a really impressive outing by them against a really good Hawaii team. They've developed some really good footballers. You see a lot of NFL influences in the schemes that they run…What you saw was a team playing with a lot of energy, physicality, resilience, and certainly closing out the game in impressive fashion…They present a lot of challenges. On offense varied tempos, multiple personnel groupings…Defensively, a very challenging third-down package…The personnel screams at you. They have big long, talented, explosive wide receivers. Big physical tight ends that can play in tight formations and open sets. Their offensive line is really impressive. They have 8 or 9 guys that can start just about anywhere. They handle a lot schematically. Only really good veteran offensive lines can handle that stuff. Just a very impressive organization."

HC Cristobal mentioned Stanford key stats: 19 of their 22 starters are either juniors or seniors Over 500 yards of offense, completed 22-34 passes for about 300 yards, 6 redzone trips, 44% on third down On defense held Hawaii to 7 three-and-outs and 40 yards rushing, total.

HC Cristobal mentioned Stanford key stats:

19 of their 22 starters are either juniors or seniors

Over 500 yards of offense, completed 22-34 passes for about 300 yards, 6 redzone trips, 44% on third down

On defense held Hawaii to 7 three-and-outs and 40 yards rushing, total.

Offensive Coordinator Shannon Dawson : "They're big. I think they've done a really good job of getting more athletic on the backend. I think their corners run really well. Hawaii throws the ball as well as anybody in the nation, and you didn't see them running wide open. Their DBs are there in the right spot, and their safeties are very aggressive…Their front, their LB's in my opinion, they take pride in not wanting you to run the football. That's obvious by how they play and the scheme they play. We have to be a physical offense to be successful in this game."

Defensive Coordinator Corey Hetherman : "It's a veteran group, especially up front. They're a disciplined team and they're very well coached…(running back) Ford is a guy we saw last year. I think he's a very talented player. Their leading rusher coming back. He runs extremely hard. He's a big back, runs behind his pads, runs through the first tackler, he creates opportunities to make the first guy miss and get some of those hidden yards that keeps you ahead of the sticks….the quarterback is a guy that's played college football. He's started 9 games, he has played in some of the biggest environments, he has some really good wins. You can tell that he has good control of the offense right now."

On having to travel to California for a Week 1 Friday game

HC Cristobal : "We have a process. We want to get your body and mind acclimated right. The travel plans resemble what we did in the postseason last year. You want to be able to practice out there. The biggest challenge is that it's a night game."

HC Cristobal : "If you analyze any schedule any year it has its challenges…they're only a big deal if you make a big deal of it as a staff…it's kind of like distractions, they're only distractions if you make them a distraction."

On Miami's team identity and expectations this season

HC Cristobal : "I don't think its fair to the former players or the current players to draw comparisons. Every team is authentic in its own way, and every team has to go out and earn their position on the college football landscape. This team will be judged at the end of the year. Right now everything we do is focused on making sure we go out and earn everything on a play-by-play basis."

HC Cristobal : "Today, one of the best plays in practice was a monster collision with Mo and Mark Fletcher. That's a very welcome thing here at the University of Miami, because if you don't practice good on good it's very hard to be your best."

On new freshmen contributing and possibly seeing playing time

HC Cristobal : "I wouldn't assume anybody of any class is going to have a significant role until we go out there and play football. It's dangerous to crown people before they hit the field and accomplish anything. It's one of the biggest issues in society nowadays…We have some [players] that mature at a more accelerated rate than others. In a world where older teams have a lot of success, we like to think there's a lot of truth to that, but in those older players you find maturity. A great example is Malachi Toney who is 18 years old, but he's mature like a 25 year old. That's one of our big focuses is whether they just got here or have been here for awhile, that their levels of maturity and professionalism are that where we can trust them and their teammates can trust them."

On having QB Darian Mensah being healthy this offseason unlike Beck last year

HC Cristobal : "The greatest ability is availability, and he's been available since January…he's gotten a ton of reps in the system, and he's such a smart guy that the autonomy that comes with this offense is something that really lends itself well to his abilities. We see a guy that's capable of doing great things, and we also see a guy that's very humble and recognizes that all that potential and ability has to be proven on a daily basis."

OC Dawson : "Last year was odd in a lot of different ways because [Beck] wasn't healthy until right towards the end of the summer, and probably not 100% for a little while just to be honest. Offense football is about chemistry, being on the same page, timing, and all the rest. So, having a guy out there that's taking those reps is vital."

On the Offensive Line and possibly being thin on the two-deep

OC Dawson : "Coach Mirabal does a phenomenal job of getting multiple people ready to play that position. He's probably the best I've been around at rotating offensive linemen throughout the course of camp, throughout the course of summer, and throughout the course of spring. We're not an operation where one guy plays one position."

Whether there is a status update on Jordan Lyle since his arrest

HC Cristobal : "Same status, letting everything run their process."

OC Dawson : "We're going to be a running back by committee, and that's been the case since I've been here. I believe in sharing the carries, I believe in sharing the abuse at that position. That position is a tough one….I don't want one guy out there all the time, and luckily enough that's probably our room that's the deepest, so we're going to utilize that room."

OC Dawson : "We're going to roll a handful of guys in there. We have a lot of depth at that position to stay fresh and see who's got the hot hand."

On dealing with up-tempo offenses like Stanford

DC Hetherman : "For us, we're going to play a lot of players. We always have. There were games where we played 24, 25, 26 guys in a game. We believe in playing a lot of players. We anticipated that we're going to get some tempo from them in the first game. They're snapping the ball with 28 seconds on the play clock, similar to SMU and South Florida. There's other times they're on the ball fast and hold the ball…It's one thing we've been working on all camp just as a defense in general."

On improvement of veteran linebacker Mo Toure

DC Hetherman : "I think the biggest thing is just the confidence of coming off an injury and having a full offseason. For the first time in awhile, after the season last year he went into winter workouts, he had spring football, he went into summer workouts, he's gone through an entire offseason for the first time since like 2021…We've been able to increase the rep load a little bit in camp, where last year early on in the season it was 'where are we going to play him, how are we going to play him.' Certain packages we may not have had him on in certain situations, and as the year on, his role grew and developed. Now we can do that early on in the season and play him in a lot of different looks."

On true freshman defensive back JJ Dunnigan

DC Hetherman : "He's had a really good camp. He had another pick today, he had three picks the other day. Early on in camp he always found the ball. The ball just seems to find him…he'll be on [special] teams early, and defensively he's going to get an opportunity to play early in the game."

articles.title: T.J. Watt changes snap counts approach to last 17-game season with Steelers
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers star T.J. Watt is adjusting his snap count management to remain fresh and preserve peak impact across a 17-game season.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are altering their defensive rotation, stepping away from the heavy starter snap counts that previously defined their outside linebacker usage.

Instead of asking star pass rushers T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith to routinely log over 80 percent of defensive snaps, Pittsburgh is implementing a deliberate four-man rotation alongside Nick Herbig and Jack Sawyer. The strategic shift aims to keep the defense's top playmakers fresh for crucial fourth-quarter situations and preserve them over a grueling 17-game regular season.

The four-man wrecking crew recently joined their teammate Cameron Heyward on his podcast, " Not Just Football with Cam Heyward ," to talk about the changes. One of the changes being implemented by new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham is a linebacker rotation aimed at keeping them fresh and healthy into the post-season.

Watt highlighted the logic behind the approach, emphasizing that speed and effort require a deep bench.

"Obviously, Jack's going to be in the fold a good amount as well because when we want to play as hard and as fast as we can, we're going to need to have a deep rotation," Watt explained.

The rotation relies heavily on mutual trust between the starters and backups. Rather than viewing rest as a concession, the unit treats quick breathers as a tactical advantage, ensuring maximum intensity on every rep.

Herbig offered a candid look at how Watt manages his energy during long, taxing drives, revealing that the veteran isn't shy about tapping out to keep the motor running high.

"'Jack, be ready, dog. Like, I'm going to need you this game, bro. I'm going to be gassed out there, bro,'" Herbig recalled Watt saying on the sideline. "'Like, we going to be on a good rotation. I can't be playing 65-plus snaps every time.'"

By giving Herbig and Sawyer immediate, high-stakes responsibilities, including critical third-down snaps, the Steelers are building a sustainable model. Managing starter workloads now ensures that when Pittsburgh needs a game-altering strip-sack in crunch time, Watt and Highsmith will have plenty left in the tank to deliver.

articles.title: Kyle Shanahan gives major update on 49ers biggest injured stars
articles.summary: Kyle Shanahan sounded optimistic about George Kittle's and Nick Bosa's chances to play Week 1 vs. the Rams in Austrialia.
articles.body:
With the San Francisco 49ers finalizing their initial 53-man roster before traveling to Australia for their Week 1 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams , head coach Kyle Shanahan provided crucial updates on All-Pro tight end George Kittle and star pass rusher Nick Bosa.

Both superstars are aiming to suit up for the season opener after spending August working back from physical setbacks. Kittle was limited to individual drills while recovering from a ruptured Achilles suffered during the postseason in January. Bosa was held out of team settings later in training camp to manage knee soreness after ramping up his activity.

Speaking on August 31, Shanahan outlined a pivotal three-day evaluation window before the team boards its flight to Melbourne.

"We're going to get them out there in these three days and hope it goes well," Shanahan said.

Because the Niners' departure schedule requires a fast-forwarded calendar, Shanahan emphasized that both core pieces will be on modified practice schedules to ensure they don't overexert themselves prior to the long flight.

"With three days before we go, we're balancing it out with both of them. We don't want them to go three days in a row," Shanahan explained. "Both of them are on a little different schedule... hopefully these three days that we have, these three practices will go the right way and make it an easy decision to get him on the plane."

Shanahan also clarified recent media speculation regarding Kittle, confirming that a phrase he used after the preseason finale was misinterpreted and that the tight end has suffered no structural setbacks.

"George has been great. He's passing everything," Shanahan noted. "There was nothing that I meant to say that people looked into. I did say that was an accident."

If both stars navigate the practice week cleanly, San Francisco expects to have its primary offensive anchor and edge rush threat fully available for Week 1.

articles.title: Former Saints draft pick gets fresh start on new team's practice squad
articles.summary: Former New Orleans Saints WR Bub Means cleared waivers but signed with the Cleveland Browns. It's a fresh start for the former fifth-round draft pick.
articles.body:
Former New Orleans Saints wide receiver Bub Means cleared waivers after being let go during Sunday's roster cuts, but he isn't staying put. Instead, Means is signing with the Cleveland Browns ' practice squad, per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler . It's a fresh start for the former fifth-round draft pick.

Means, 25, flashed potential through a couple of years in New Orleans but just couldn't stay healthy. His 2024 rookie year ended on injured reserve, and a preseason injury cut short his 2025 follow-up before it got off the ground. He's healthy now, though, and hoping to stand out in a new environment. Cleveland drafted wide receivers in both the first (KC Concepcion) and second rounds (Denzel Boston) while bringing back Jerry Jeudy, Isaiah Bond, Malachi Corley, and Tylan Wallace. That's a solid receiving corps even with a shaky quarterback situation.

The Saints will host the Browns on Sunday, Nov. 8, coming out of their bye week and a road trip to face the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris. Maybe Means will be in the opposing lineup.

articles.title: Hidden Yardage: The most important stat for Kentucky
articles.summary: Kentucky faces Youngstown State, but the real test is mastering field position to prepare for Alabama.
articles.body:
Most fans watching Kentucky football open its 2026 season against Youngstown State on Sep. 5 will track the usual numbers: passing yards, third-down conversions, and explosive plays. The number that actually predicts how the Wildcats fare against Alabama seven days later won't show up in those columns. It's Average Starting Field Position (ASFP)—the least glamorous, most decisive stat in football.

Football is a territory game before it's anything else. Starting a drive at your own 20 instead of your own 35 barely registers in isolation. Multiply that gap across a 12-drive game, though, and a +15 ASFP edge is worth 180 yards — nearly two full fields — generated entirely by the interplay between Will Stein's offense and Jay Bateman's defense.

This isn't the usual season-opening layup, either. Youngstown State comes in off an 8-5 season and an FCS playoff berth under seventh-year coach Doug Phillips, and the Penguins return quarterback Beau Brungard and All-American left tackle Desmeal Leigh, the backbone of an attack that gave FCS defenses matchup problems all last season. Kentucky beat this same program 31-0 back in 2022, but that YSU team was still building. This one enters Lexington expected to contend for the Missouri Valley title—which makes it a sharper field-position measuring stick than a typical Week 1 body-bag game.

Kentucky should still win comfortably. The way they win the field-position battle is what will tell us whether they're ready for Alabama .

Jay Bateman doesn't call a defense built to survive—he calls one built to dictate. Sitting back in a passive shell isn't a viable plan against SEC-caliber offensive lines, and it isn't Bateman's plan.

That front seven won't get a freebie, either. Youngstown State returns Leigh, an All-American, anchoring a veteran offensive line—which means push on early downs has to be earned, not assumed. Every tackle for loss Bateman's front generates against that group does double duty: it kills a Penguins drive now, and it rehearses the exact sequence Kentucky will need to force a punt from deep in Alabama territory next week. A three-and-out or a turnover doesn't just stop the opponent—it hands Stein's offense has a shorter field to work with.

The number to watch: if Kentucky's defense pins Youngstown State to an average starting position near their own 20, or forces enough short fields that Kentucky itself starts drives near midfield, the scheme is doing its job. A shorter field means Stein's playbook only has to produce two first downs to reach range.

Stein's offense has a job that has nothing to do with scoring. Even on drives that stall, if the offense is consistently picking up two or three first downs — moving the ball from the 25 to the 45 before punting — that's the offense protecting its own defense, not just failing to finish.

Watch the drives Saturday that don't end in points. Is Kentucky flipping the field? Youngstown State's roster questions this year are mostly on defense, which makes it a fair test rather than a gimme: if Stein's unit can routinely push a defense still finding itself back near its own goal line, that's the same discipline that matters against Alabama. Force a Crimson Tide offense to sustain 10-play, 85-yard drives instead of 5-play, 40-yard ones, and the odds of a holding call, a drop, or a sack climb with every additional snap.

Track where every drive starts Saturday, not just how it ends.

Warning sign: Kentucky's ASFP sits inside their own 25 while a Youngstown State team with a returning All-American tackle and an FCS playoff pedigree is routinely starting near its own 35. Losing the hidden-yardage battle to a quality FCS opponent is a red flag Alabama's talent gap will expose.

Good sign: Stein's offense avoids negative plays on early downs to pin the Penguins deep, and Bateman's front — against a real offensive line, not a pushover — still forces short fields that hand Kentucky the ball near midfield. That's the formula working as designed.

Alabama will likely still hold the talent edge. Field position is the lever Kentucky has to close that gap, and a Youngstown State team good enough to matter is exactly the opponent to prove it against. Week 1 is the only tape they'll get before it does.

articles.title: Mudryk a deadline day alternative to Ndiaye for Tottenham
articles.summary: Tottenham could be set for a busy end to the summer transfer window, with reports suggesting they have agreed deals with Chelsea for attacker Mykhailo Mudryk...
articles.body:
Tottenham could be set for a busy end to the summer transfer window, with reports suggesting they have agreed deals with Chelsea for attacker Mykhailo Mudryk and defender Tosin Adarabioyo.

The Press Association understands Spurs made an enquiry to Chelsea over Mudryk, who has only recently returned to football after resolving his doping case with the Football Association but worked with manager Roberto De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk.

According to reports, Spurs have also moved for Adarabioyo, who joined Chelsea from Fulham in 2024.

De Zerbi had originally set his sights on Liverpool forward Cody Gakpo before Manchester City stole a march, which forced Tottenham to target Everton winger Iliman Ndiaye.

However, City also turned their attention to Ndiaye after Liverpool refused to sanction the sale of Gakpo and the Senegal attacker appears set to move to the Etihad Stadium, with a fee worth up to £65million agreed with Everton.

And that development has turn prompted a switch of focus to Mudryk, who could now link up with old boss De Zerbi in a loan move before Tuesday's 11pm deadline.

The deals would continue Spurs remarkable summer window after young forward Mikey Moore finally joined Bundesliga side Cologne on loan for the remainder of the season on Monday.

That deal was agreed at the start of August but Spurs' difficulty in landing attacking targets meant Moore started the club's first two games and he scored against Charlton.

PA understands Moore's move is a straight loan with no option or obligation to make the move permanent.

Richarlison is free to leave Spurs after the north London club brought in Savio and Omar Marmoush from Manchester City last week, but has other options alongside an emotional transfer back to Everton.

Brazil forward Richarlison released a statement on Monday that warned "never again will anyone decide my future for me", but said: "If they reach an agreement between Spurs and Everton, I will return to my beloved club."

Midfielder Pape Sarr is expected to seal a loan to Juventus before the deadline after an agreement with the Serie A club was reached.

Sarr will join Juventus on an initial season-long loan and the move will become permanent for an overall package of €30 million ($34.8 million) if certain obligations are met during the 2026-27 campaign.

Kevin Danso was not included in Tottenham's matchday squad for Saturday's 2-0 home defeat to Newcastle after De Zerbi revealed he asked to leave.

Sunderland had a loan bid rejected for Danso on Friday night, but any departure of the Austria international would leave Spurs with only four senior centre-backs.

Young Brazil left-back Souza is set to depart on loan to Porto and Japanese defender Kota Takai is primed to join Belgium outfit Sint-Truidense for the rest of the campaign.

There is interest in Tottenham under-21 players Alfie Dorrington, James Rowswell, Tyrese Hall and Damola Ajayi, who are all expected to link up with EFL clubs.

Spurs academy graduate Callum Olusesi will stay and continue his rehabilitation after a spell on the sidelines and 17-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett will remain with De Zerbi's senior squad after an excellent pre-season.

articles.title: Everton agree £40m deal for US star striker Folarin Balogun from Monaco
articles.summary: Everton have agreed a £40m deal with Monaco for United States striker Folarin Balogun as they look to strengthen their attack before Tuesday’s transfer deadl...
articles.body:
Everton have agreed a £40m deal with Monaco for United States striker Folarin Balogun as they look to strengthen their attack before Tuesday's transfer deadline.

According to a report from the BBC, Balogun, 25, has been a key target for the Toffees after they pushed ahead with their interest despite also exploring a deal for former striker Richarlison.

The Brazilian had been involved in a proposed move from Tottenham, but personal terms could not be agreed with Everton, leaving the club to pursue Balogun instead.

Folarin Balogun set to join Everton for £40m

Balogun joined Monaco from boyhood club Arsenal in 2023 and has scored 31 goals in 91 appearances across all competitions for the Ligue 1 side.

He has also established himself as an important player for the USA, scoring 12 goals in 31 international appearances.

The striker was also at the centre of controversy during this summer's World Cup after being sent off for serious foul play against Bosnia-Herzegovina in the last 32.

Despite being expected to serve an automatic suspension, FIFA's disciplinary committee suspended his ban for a year, allowing Balogun to feature in the USA's last-16 defeat by Belgium.

UEFA described the decision as 'unprecedented, incomprehensible and unjustifiable'.

Balogun scored three goals during the tournament and will now be looking ahead to a new chapter in the Premier League.

Everton's move comes after their plans for Richarlison collapsed, while Iliman Ndiaye's proposed switch to Tottenham also fell through before Manchester City agreed a deal worth up to £65m.

With the deadline approaching, Everton have moved quickly for Balogun and the £40m agreement gives them the attacking addition they wanted.
