articles.title: Jon Sumrall previews Florida's season opener against FAU
articles.summary: Jon Sumrall previewed Florida's season opener against FAU and discussed the Gators' depth chart, young players, team leadership and injuries.
articles.body:
Jon Sumrall met with reporters Monday as the Florida Gators shifted their focus from fall camp to their season opener against the FAU Owls.

Sumrall discussed the emotions surrounding his debut as Florida's head coach, the challenge FAU presents and the importance of creating a strong home-field advantage inside the Swamp. He also addressed the team's first depth chart, the development of several freshmen and the leadership that emerged during camp.

The Gators' coach also shared his thoughts on Florida's coordinators, the changing college football calendar, his game-day music and the team's injury situation entering Week 1.

Game week. Exciting. Obviously. Do all this work all year to play football games and look forward to watching our guys go compete and put their hard work to use.

Got a really good opponent in FAU. Played them last year when I was at Tulane. Explosive. Offensively, I think the 15th- or 16th-most production returning in college football.

You look at the quarterback. He's played a lot of football. Really experienced, a big guy with a good arm. He can make all the throws, and he runs a little bit better than you think.

Receiving corps, they've got some really good players. This number eight sticks out from last year to me. He's a guy they target a lot and makes a lot of plays. But they've got other good players around him.

They've added good pieces through the transfer portal at tight end. The running back room they have is good. The O-line is solid. They do a nice job operating within their scheme.

Then defensively, that number one, I remember him being a game-wrecker last year on the D-line when we played them. I felt like he was a problem, and they're really well coached across the board.

They're good in special teams. I think that's probably something that doesn't get talked about enough. They were top 40 in every special teams category that we evaluate last year, so that's an area where we have to be dialed in and well prepared.

But excited to watch our guys go play. We need, man, we need an unbelievable home-field advantage. When I went through the process of taking this job, I remember playing here in 2004 and how electric the venue is. We need it to be that way every time we play at home.

We play this Saturday night. There shouldn't be an empty seat, and we need Gator Nation to turn out and support our guys. If we want an elite-level program, which I think we all want, it takes everybody. It takes the fans, it takes the coaches, it takes the players, it takes everybody.

We need Saturday night to feel like we want to be a top-20, top-10 team, a playoff team. That's our goal and our vision, and it needs to feel like that every time we play in that stadium. I look forward to hopefully seeing that crowd Saturday night embrace our football team. Our guys have already put in a lot of work.

Monday through Friday, I tell people this all the time around our building: those are my days. Saturday is the players' day, and I can't wait to watch them go play Saturday night.

What is your excitement level for your debut as Florida's head coach in The Swamp?

I'll be amped. But the day is not about me. Never will be. Like I said, coaches' days to me are Sunday through Friday. We coach the hell out of our players all the time.

If you're not fortunate enough to be at practice, today on the offensive field, I mean, they were coaching everything. The defensive field, everything. Special teams, I lost my mind in the special teams period at one point because I saw something I didn't like.

Our guys are getting coached every play, every day, Sunday through Friday. Saturday, I want it to be about the players. Yeah, I'll get critiqued when things don't go well. I'm fine there, and we'll get credit when they go good, whatever.

But Saturday, game day, at that point you've coached them. They don't rise to the occasion. I think they fall to the level of their training. I want them to be so trained that Saturday night they can go cut it loose and play the game the right way.

For me personally, I will be excited. I'm excited every time we play. I don't care if we're playing in a parking lot. I'm excited. I don't care who the opponent is. I'm excited. It's an opportunity you get. I told our team this morning, you get 12 regular-season games.

I had another — I'm not going to say who — colleague this summer say, "I don't know. You can't get your team up for all 12 games." I'm like, "Well, maybe you can't, but if you can't get up for all 12 games, you've got a problem."

To me, you work so daggum hard. I'll be really excited about the opportunity to watch our team go play and all the work that's been put in. Go cut it loose.

What does it mean to return to The Swamp as Florida's head coach 22 years after playing there?

It's funny, I talked to my head college coach from my last two years on Saturday afternoon. Rich Brooks was the head coach at Oregon from 1977 to '94. The field at Oregon is named after Coach Brooks. It's Autzen Stadium, but it's Rich Brooks Field.

Coach Brooks was my college head coach in '03 and for my last two years as a player. Every time we talk, I kid around with him. In 2004, he almost got fired because he was starting guys like me, right?

But I called him just to tell him thank you. I said, "Coach, it's crazy to think that 22 years ago I was playing in this stadium as a below-average linebacker in this league, and now I'm getting to coach as a head coach in this stadium, in this venue, at this program."

I just wanted him to know, without you, I wouldn't be here. There are a lot of people who have helped me get to where I am. I haven't gotten here on my own. Now, don't discredit it. I've worked really, really hard to be here.

But there are so many people who have invested in me, either as a young person coming up in this game or as a coach. There are a ton of people who have helped me get to this point. I'll think about a lot of those people this week because I do every year in Game 1. I think about all the people who have helped me become the football person I am.

What did mock game week accomplish, and what needs to be cleaned up before Saturday?

Yeah, mock game week is as much about everybody understanding the battle rhythms, as I like to call it. The rhythm and the routine of how you get ready for a Saturday game.

Today is Monday practice. Our guys experienced last Monday what that looked like. Tomorrow is Tuesday practice. They understand what it looks like and the flow of meetings and the operation of how we install.

I wanted last week to run through as many of the scenarios that come up during a game week as possible to eliminate the clutter or the mishaps. We're going to make mistakes Saturday night. I can promise you. I've never been part of a Game 1 where there weren't plenty of them.

I showed our team all the Week 0 games. I showed 20 plays this morning. There was one game where there were 12 guys on the field for a field-goal block three times in the same game on Saturday.

I'm not going to act like we're perfect, but I'm going to dang sure try to make sure we get 11 guys on the field. We're going to work our tails off. We do all those things to try to make sure we get the processes done right, the pregame warmup done right and a lot of those things so that guys don't have to think.

One of the things I thought was really cool was that last Friday we had Justin Gaethje talk to the team, the UFC fighter and lightweight champion of the world in UFC right now. One of the answers he gave about his preparation was that he wanted to be so prepared that when you're in the ring, when you're in the Octagon, you don't think. You just do.

"I don't have to think about what I'm doing. I'm so trained, I just do it because it's what I do."

I wanted our guys last week to go through those rhythms. This week, they're not thinking, "What time is the special teams meeting?" or "What time is this?" or "What time is that?" or "How does the practice flow?" They understand.

That way, hopefully, Saturday we've taken some of the extra thought out of what goes into playing the game. They can go cut it loose, play and have fun with it.

How do you handle depth-chart conversations so players are not blindsided?

We're really, really direct. I don't hide things from our players. I'm really honest. My wife would tell you that's one of my greatest strengths and maybe one of my greatest weaknesses. I'm going to tell you the truth.

If you like the truth, you're going to love being around me. If you don't like the truth, you're going to hate being around me. Everybody on our depth chart, wherever they are, knows why. There are no surprises. We take things head-on.

I think the players deserve that. They put in too much time and too much work not to have real conversations with them. You get what you earn in this game. You want to play more? Practice great. When you get your opportunities in games, if you want to play more after that, play well in the game and you'll get to play more.

What have Lacota Dippre and Florida's tight ends done to earn their roles?

Yeah, Lacota has been really, really steady all training camp. He's been really consistent his entire time here.

I'm fired up about what he's done just from a consistency standpoint, day in and day out. The way he shows up is very impressive. Behind him, I think Heze has made as much improvement for a freshman as anybody on our team since January.

In January, I would have told you there was a low-percentage chance Heze Kent was going to be ready to compete and play this year. Then, through the summer, I'm like, "Okay, this guy's got a shot." During training camp, he just got better.

The other two, Amir and Luke, they both have done some good things in their own right, unique to how they play the position and the game. Then the other one is (Evan) Chieca. He's back moving around at practice. I'm not sure about his availability for Saturday yet. It's not off the table, but it's not a green light yet. But he's there.

Which freshmen have made the biggest strides entering the season?

Yeah, I think K.J. Ford had a really good spring. I think sometimes, as a freshman, you can hit a wall. He hit a little bit of a wall maybe early in training camp and then responded during the last week of training camp, which I was pleased with.

There are a lot of guys who have helped themselves. We are going to play players we trust, so there are not going to be a ton of them playing right out of the gate. There are a few. K.J., I think, will play Saturday night. I want to play as many freshmen as are ready to play.

I think you'll see some of them who maybe aren't on that two-deep elevate as the year goes on, and then others will have big special teams roles. CJ Bronaugh is one. CJ was out during the spring. When he's been available, he's flashed as a player who I think has a high ceiling and really good potential.

He was probably just a little bit behind because he was out all spring. If he had been available all spring, I think he probably would be closer to prime-time action in regard to where the depth chart sits.

How have you evolved as a head coach since your first game week at Troy?

There are some routines that have stayed the same, and there are some things I think you constantly adapt and evolve. I'm more comfortable than Year 1. In Year 1, there were probably some things coming that I wasn't fully prepared for mentally. Now, I think I see what's coming a lot further out.

But the routines are pretty similar. A lot of the things we do are very clockwork, if you will. Personally, I've shared this with y'all before, but I'm very regimented. My schedule does not deviate. Every Monday is the same. Every Tuesday is the same. Every Wednesday is the same. I think that way you understand how to be prepared by game time.

But there are some things that have evolved and changed in how we do things, just to be smarter with maybe a couple of practice-model things we do.

Have you learned to trust your assistants more as a head coach?

Yeah, there's a lot to that. My first year as a head coach at Troy, I thought I had to have my hand in everything all the time. I was probably a miserable guy to work for. Now, I think I've done a better job. We're at practice, and I can look at the call sheet on offense, defense or in the kicking game, and I know what we've got going on.

I'll interject with the coordinator here and there. I'll ask him, "Hey, what's our thought process there?" But now I let them do their thing a little bit more and probably take their feedback better.

We had kind of a cool experience, I guess it's been two weeks ago now. Training camp is a blur. We had a head coaches meeting with all the head coaches in the athletic department and had a chance to hear from Billy Donovan. It was a really cool experience for me because I think he's an unbelievable coach.

He said something that really resonated with me in that meeting a couple of weeks ago. He said, "As the head coach, you have to make the final decision always, but you're never smarter than the room. Take the feedback from the room and then make a really good, educated decision to move forward."

For me, if I'm smarter than the entire room, then we've got a really bad staff. I want to have great people in the room who challenge me and help me think outside the box a little bit or maybe bring up ideas, whether it's Buster, Brad or an analyst. I don't care who it is.

Then, yeah, I have to make the decision about exactly how we're going to do something moving forward. It was such spot-on advice at that time because it was a couple of weeks ago. I'm like, "What a great reminder.' As we get ready to enter the season, take the feedback of the room. Yeah, you've got to make the final decision, but listen to the room.

PHOTOS: Highlights from Florida football's win over FAU Owls in 2021

How will the experience of Brad White and Buster Faulkner benefit the team this season?

Well, you want people you trust, and I trust both of those guys because they've got great experience and they're both really qualified in the way they carry themselves; they're good men and they're good at what they do.

Going back to what I just said, they're not ego guys or prideful. They want to trust the people in their rooms, so they're going to take the feedback. We've got a solid staff from top to bottom. If you're Buster, you can look around the room and there are a lot of quality people to lean on in that entire room. It's the same thing for Brad.

For me as a head coach, I have guys who are really well equipped to do a great job in their roles and great people around them to support them. I know and trust that those guys who are coordinating will listen to the feedback their rooms give them.

How helpful is the familiarity of facing an opponent you played last season?

Yeah, there's some familiarity, which is helpful. It's not like we're playing a team where we have no awareness of anything about them. I would have been okay if we had scheduled a less talented team for Game 1. These guys are well coached, man.

I think Zach does a phenomenal job. Kittley is a really good football coach, and he's got a great staff. There are some challenges. They were the fastest offense in college football last year. They went for it on fourth down more than anybody in college football last year.

I think, in Game 1, if I'm not mistaken, they went for it nine times in the first game against Maryland last year. Nine. The first drive of the game last year when we played them at Tulane was at our place. You blinked, and they were inside the red zone. You're like, "What happened? How did they get here so fast?" They're really good.

There's some familiarity that maybe helps, but I don't think you can simulate some of the things they do in practice, no matter how hard you try. Their tempo is so fast. Whatever the fastest is, they're faster because they were No. 1 in the country.

There are some nice things about at least knowing some things about them. They know some things about us, too.

Why do you support Commissioner Greg Sankey's stance on adding players after the deadline?

Well, yeah. I'm a head coach in the SEC, so I'm going to abide by what the SEC wants me to abide by. That's my stance on what Commissioner Sankey did. Number two, our add/drop date for academics here has passed.

While our guys get paid and there's all this other stuff now, you still have to be enrolled in classes. It's too late to get enrolled in classes here. It would be against the rules because they wouldn't be the student part of student-athlete here. We can't get them into classes.

I'm always about, "How do you make your team better?" I referenced it, I think, on Finebaum or maybe with y'all, but I added Jake Retzlaff to my roster at Tulane last year, I think, July 27. I'm all for having a good player whenever I can get a good player. But there are some barriers to us adding a good player.

One of them is that I'm going to follow the rules of what our commissioner said. We also can't get a guy into classes right now. I think if you were an NFL player, you're an NFL player. If you're a college player, you're a college player.

Our roster was set a while ago to move forward, and there was no loophole to add a player. Now, if it's legal and approved and all that, that's a different deal. But our league has said they're against it. If our league is against it, I'm going to follow the rules and the leadership of our conference and our university.

Will you have any nerves or butterflies Saturday?

I'll just be excited. I don't get nervous. If I see a rattlesnake, I might get nervous. But I'm fired up to let our guys go cut it loose and play. I still get amped, but I'm not biting my fingernails or anything.

How do you manage expectations surrounding Florida entering the season?

My expectation is to try to go 1-0 this week. That's my thought process every week. It's, "How do you win that week?" At the end of the week, Saturday night or Sunday morning, I hope we're 1-0. Whatever happens this week, we'll review it, we'll flush it and then we'll do the same thing the next week.

I think it's great for fans and maybe the media to go, "Well, this would be a good year." I don't have time to do that. A good year to me is when you win every game you play. Win them all, and it's a good year. Win a championship, and that's a great year.

I think you can limit what you accomplish when you start to go, "Well, this would be good enough." I think you start to put maybe some undue pressure on yourself when you're like, "Well, this is what the benchmark needs to be." I think when you have really high standards — "standards" is a word I use a lot — things usually work out for you.

But the expectation at Florida is championships in every sport, not just football. That's part of what drew me here. We've got a lot of work to do to be a championship-caliber program day in and day out. We're working hard at it, but I just want to do whatever we can this week to go 1-0.

I know there are certain scoreboard outcomes that people would love to say define success. Success to me is 1-0 every week. If we go 1-0 every week, I think everybody would be really damn happy.

What did Ben Hanks do to earn a starting role, and what is the secondary's biggest challenge this week?

Ben has done a great job going back to the whole time I've been here. He's worked really hard. He's got good length and can run. He plays the ball in the air well. He's got good ball skills. He's a guy who works incredibly hard.

I was in the weight room this morning at 6 a.m. with Rusty, and he was in there doing mobility when meetings weren't until 7. He was on his own. He's a guy who is invested in his craft. I'm excited to see him play a more prominent role.

He played a little bit last year. I think he played in four games, but he'll play a bigger role. For that entire secondary, the vertical shots, the tempo, getting lined up, communicating and eye discipline are important. Like I said, they'll throw the ball all over the place and throw it down the field a lot. They're going to take shots, and you've got to stay on top in coverage.

When you get an opportunity to make a play on the ball, you've got to make a play. When they catch the ball, get them on the ground and let's move to the next play. We have to try to limit the explosive plays because that's one thing they do at a really high level. They create explosives.

What has Buster Faulkner done as expected, and how has he pleasantly surprised you?

What he's done that I hoped he would do is constantly evolve. He's looking at what fits our people and how to tailor the system to the player. That's what I already knew.

I think Buster has done a really good job, going back to the earlier question about the difference between me in Year 1 and Year 4 or 5. Buster has brought some good big-picture ideas to me, program-wise, that we've been able to implement. A lot of them were in the summer program or spring, about certain walkthrough patterns they had done or that he liked doing. I think that fits how he wants to do it.

The thing he's done that I'm really grateful for is that he's upfront and honest and speaks about what he thinks is going to help us. He's not a yes-man. He and I will go back and forth, and I like that. I don't like for somebody, when I say something, to just go, "Yes, sir," and move on.

I want him to go, "Have you thought about it like this?" Then I go, "Oh, you know what? I hadn't. That's a good idea. Let's talk about that." I've appreciated the dialogue he and I have had about how to do everything we can to put our team in a position to be successful.

What was your reaction to the proposed calendar changes and reduction in preseason practices?

We've become an all-year training model. It used to be that, in the summers, if you brought out a football, that was an NCAA violation. Now we get two hours a week of football time. That's different.

Our player movement hasn't just looked more like the NFL. We've gone past the NFL, where it's year to year for every player. In the NFL, you have contracts that are four or five years. Ours are like everything is a one-year deal. The model has evolved.

COVID created some of that because we were all in the middle of spring practice in 2020. COVID shut everything down that March. When we got back in the summer, when all the guys came back to campus, they allowed us to do more football with the guys ahead of training camp.

Now we get to training camp, and by the time we do Install 1, I'm like, "I feel like this is the ninth time we've gone through Install 1." I think it makes sense. The best ability any of us have in life is availability.

The old-school training camp model that I participated in 20-something years ago, where you practiced three times a day, may have made you tough. I don't know that it made you healthy for Game 1. I remember my first collegiate start; I think it was 2002 or '03 against Louisville. I remember thinking, "Golly, I'm tired today," because I had just been chewed up during training camp.

I think now we're making decisions about our practice models, the flow of the year and the calendar that are about player health, welfare and safety. This is still a tough, physical game. You have to do things in a certain manner to be prepared to play it the right way. But you need to be smart tough, not dumb tough.

With the 21 practice opportunities, I've already thought through it. I've had enough foresight that this was coming that, for the last year, I've put some things to paper about what I think this looks like for us. With Week 0 in the future becoming Week 1, really, and everybody having two byes throughout the year, training camp will now be one week shorter.

There are a lot of things I've already thought about. Even though I am focused on this week, I also think about next year, the next year and the next year. If you wait until it's right in front of you, you're behind. I've spent some time thinking about what that looks like.

Is the mock game week schedule designed to help players enter Saturday healthier and fresher?

Yeah, I do think our training camp schedule is helpful for them. The work is the work. You're going to practice, you're going to wear full gear on certain days, and you've got to bang. But you've also got to know how to go up and down a little bit with how you're pushing them.

The mock game week is a little bit about getting them back, but it's also about getting them ready for the week. There's comfortability with the format. They have an expectation of what it looks like.

Do you have a go-to song or artist on game day?

I've got a few artists. I like AC/DC, and then I love — this is probably not most people's pump-up music — Chris Stapleton. I listen to Chris Stapleton probably every day of my life, even on game day.

Which players have emerged as leaders entering Week 1?

Myles Graham has been really, really steady as a leader.

Brendan Bett, I'm probably as proud of him as anybody because he had a choice a year ago after the South Florida game. It could have gone a couple of different ways. He's really elevated and responded to maybe a mistake with, I think, a mature approach. He's been a positive, elder-statesman leader in that room.

Jayden Woods is a tremendous leader. Aaron Chiles is a good leader. Bryce Thornton, D.J. Coleman and the whole receiving corps. I was telling somebody the other day, for us to have Dallas Wilson, VB3, Eric Singleton and Micah Mays in that room, and Bailey Stockton, TJ Abrams and more, and to have a receiver room like that where nobody is a jerk is unheard of.

Usually, you have a receiver room like that and somebody is going to be a jerk to deal with. I like coaching all those guys every day. They're fun to be around. They always have a smile on their face. They're ultimate team guys.

Harrison Moore has stepped up as a leader. TJ Shanahan, Lacota Dippre, Philo and Tramell — there are a lot of guys.I think you guys have been able to see that Philo and Tramell are both really comfortable in their own skin. They've shown a lot of leadership by how they handled the process of the quarterback competition, whatever it was. It gets named a competition, but guys are competing all the time for playing time, right? They handled that process really well. They led by how they carried out that process.

There's a long list of guys on our team who I think have elevated their leadership.

How has Khaleil Jackson responded to his opportunity to return and earn a role?

This place means a lot to Khaleil. He's a legacy player here. His family has a great history in this program. He's a really hardworking guy.

Coming off the lower-body extremity injuries he had most recently, I think one thing that has helped him a ton is that he committed to getting his body as lean as possible. When you get heavier, your knees, ankles and all the joints below your waist are going to take more of a toll.

He's leaned up. He's gotten lighter, which has allowed him to make himself more available. He hasn't missed a practice all training camp. I do think he's going to have a role in how we're going to play the game. I'm excited to see him have an opportunity to put all his hard work out there.

He's been a really positive impact in how he carries himself day in and day out.

We're pretty healthy. I've been opening with the training report or the injury report just so you guys know I'm being transparent with you.

Chieca is questionable. He's practicing. He's running around, but it's a matter of how far we want to push him. Extending Kelvin (Jimenez), as I hit on, he is out for the year. Kendall Guervil is back practicing.

The injury report is pretty positive in regard to having pretty much everybody ready to go.

articles.title: British Open: Wu Yize to face Kyren Wilson in second round
articles.summary: World champion Wu Yize sets up a tie against Kyren Wilson at the British Open, with many big names progressing through round one in Cheltenham.
articles.body:
World champion Wu Yize set up an intriguing second-round tie against former Crucible winner Kyren Wilson at the British Open after both won their opening matches.

China's Wu beat compatriot Liu Hongyu 4-3 in Cheltenham, while 2024 world champion Wilson was a 4-1 winner against Austria's Florian Nuessle.

Last year's British Open champion Shaun Murphy was joined by Ding Junhui, Barry Hawkins, Judd Trump and John Higgins in progressing to the second round.

However, three-time world champion Mark Williams lost 4-0 to David Gilbert, world number two Neil Robertson fell 4-1 to Pang Junxu, and 2023 world champion Luca Brecel fell 4-3 to Chris Wakelin.

Mark Joyce, who replaced Ronnie O'Sullivan after the seven-time world champion withdrew because of medical reasons, beat Poland's Mateusz Baranowski 4-1.

New world number one Zhao Xintong, the first Chinese player to become world champion in 2025, will play his opening-round match against England's Oliver Brown on Tuesday.

Zhao reached the final of the Wuhan Open last week, securing the top ranking spot in the process, only to lose 10-7 to countryman Chang Bingyu in the title match.

The British Open uses a random draw for each round, with no seeds, meaning high-profile names can face each other early in the tournament.

articles.title: Texas Tech's Joey McGuire takes shot at USC crowd
articles.summary: Joey McGuire said Aug. 31 that Texas Tech fans will 'show up, no matter what the weather's like,' throwing a jab at USC's Week 0 crowd.
articles.body:
Texas Tech football coach Joey McGuire started his response to reporters on Monday, Aug. 31 by noting his respect for Southern California coach Lincoln Riley, before then seemingly calling out the Trojans ' fanbase for the small crowd at USC's Week 0 win over San Jose State.

The No. 14 Trojans defeated San Jose State 42-26 on Saturday, Aug. 29 in front of an almost-empty crowd at Los Angeles Memorial Stadium, due to unusual humidity in the area paired with low interest in a Week 0 game against a lower-tier Mountain West opponent.

McGuire said that won't be the case when Texas Tech faces Abilene Christian on Sept. 5 in Lubbock, Texas.

"Not to take any shots, because I have a lot of respect for USC and Lincoln Riley, but it's really awesome to be playing in Lubbock, Texas, knowing we're going to be playing in front of 60,000 (fans)," McGuire said Monday. "It's going to be warm. It's going to be every bit as warm as it was Saturday.

"The great thing is we got some really tough people in West Texas that love their football and they're going to show up, no matter what the weather's like. There's not going to be any excuse of why they're not going to be here for us."

Riley, who grew up in Muleshoe, Texas, a small town in West Texas, played quarterback for the Red Raiders and was an assistant there from 2003-2009 under Mike Leach. The crowd at USC has become a talking point across college football in recent days, especially with the program's status as an historic college football power.

USC is expecting increased attendance moving forward in the season, it said in a statement to USA TODAY Sports .

"We understand the factors that impacted Saturday's attendance," the school wrote. "We have high expectations and a premier home schedule this season, and we know the competitive advantage an electric Coliseum atmosphere can provide our program. We thank our fans who showed up Saturday and look forward to seeing increased attendance the rest of the season."

McGuire prefaced his comment by saying "not to take any shots," but ended up making the rounds on social media, instead.

articles.title: Reports: Juventus eye Nicolás Tagliafico if Juan Cabal heads to Atalanta on Deadline Day
articles.summary: One South American left back could come in the another if things happen on the final day of the summer mercato.
articles.body:
Juventus are expected to have a busy Deadline Day on Tuesday, but mostly because of the fact that multiple players who they have agreed to bring in on loan will be putting pen to paper on their contracts for the 2026-27 season. There is, however, one final combination of potential deals that are very much connected and could see one final change to Juve's defense.

According to IlBianconero's Romeo Agresti and TuttoJuve's Mirko Di Natale among others, Juventus have had talks with Nicolás Tagliafico's camp over the current Lyon left back's willingness to leave Ligue 1 and head to Italy on the final day summer transfer window. That is, of course, if Juventus and Atalanta are able to agree to a deal for Juan Cabal, who is being sought by the same director who brought him to Turin two years ago, Cristiano Giuntoli.

Juventus are still waiting on an offer for Cabal from Atalanta, according to Di Natale. La Dea have seen multiple fullbacks head to the Premier League over the course of the summer transfer window, and have been one of the least active clubs in Serie A this summer, signing just two players and spending all of €14 million as of Monday.

Cabal being linked with a move to Atalanta has been looked on and then off and now on again over the last handful of days. Juventus have been trying to offload the Colombian left back who had a rough second season in Turin all summer long, with a move to Bologna first being discussed at the same time in which they were negotiating for Jhon Lucumí. That, oviously, never materialized and Cabal heads into the final hours of the transfer window still somewhat uncertain about where he will be playing once the window closes.

Tagliafico would be a much more experienced option compared to Cabal, although what he has left at age 34 is probably a reasonable thought. He is coming off a run to the World Cup final with Argentina, starting the extra-time loss to Spain and being matched up against one of the best talents in the world today, Lamine Yamal.

He has been at Lyon since 2022 after moving to Ligue 1 following a four-year spell with Ajax.

articles.title: Raiders send WR Dont'e Thornton to IR and bring veteran LB back
articles.summary: The moves continued Monday as the Raiders placed second-year WR Dont'e Thornton on IR and brought back a veteran LB they had cut.
articles.body:
Monday afternoon, a day after having officially announced all their cuts, the Raiders made another move. The team announced that WR Dont'e Thornton will head to injured reserve.

Thornton has been injured through much of camp and for several weeks now head coach Klint Kubiak has said he expects Thornton to return soon. First he expected he would be back during the preseason, and then on Friday, he said this about the second-year receiver.

"He's still working to come back from an injury, working really hard at it too. And that's part of football, injuries are part of football, and he's straining to get better to get back on the field."

Thornton's exact injury is not known. They certainly haven't known the severity of it up to this point. But it seems like this was the plan yesterday when he made the roster.

With the roster cuts, the one unexpected one was LB Segun Olubi. The special teams maven was the one player on my 53-man roster projection who was cut. And now we see why. Because the plan was to then turn around and sign him back. Only a risk if Olubi wanted to go elsewhere because he wasn't subject to waivers as a vested veteran.

Olubi was signed this offseason after four seasons with the Colts . Last season, he played in all 17 games and recorded 11 special teams tackles, one forced fumble and one blocked punt. That blocked punt came against the Raiders.

The 6-0, 225-pound linebacker appeared in 51 games in Indianapolis registering 30 tackles on special teams, the most on the Colts team over that span.

articles.title: BREAKING: UCLA AD Jarmond fired, replaced by former Lakers executive
articles.summary: "UCLA Athletics currently carries a significant financial deficit, and its current path is not sustainable," stated UCLA chancellor Julio Frenk.
articles.body:
The Martin Jarmond era at UCLA has come to an abrupt ending.

According to California Post senior college sports reporter Ben Bolch, the former Bruins athletic director was fired Monday afternoon, days before kickoff of a new college football season. Jarmond is immediately being replaced by former Los Angeles Lakers executive Tim Harris, who "will serve as athletic director and CEO of the athletic department on a pro bono basis effective immediately," per Bolch's exclusive report .

UCLA chancellor Julio Frenk shared the news within the university's community, which he characterized as a "new path forward for UCLA Athletics," in a written statement acquired by Bolch.

"We have all watched as the landscape of college athletics has transformed in recent years, driven by the introduction of Name, Image and Likeness (NIL), new models for student-athlete compensation and a rapidly changing sports marketplace. UCLA must have an athletics model that leads — not just keeps pace," Frenk stated. "UCLA Athletics currently carries a significant financial deficit, and its current path is not sustainable. Now is the moment to build a model for athletics that protects the breadth of our program, creates new opportunities for student-athletes and coaches, and supports itself through the revenue it generates."

The Bruins football team starts the 2026 campaign Saturday night in Berkeley against the California Golden Bears.

articles.title: John Harbaugh breaks down decisions made on Giants' initial 53-man roster
articles.summary: Following Monday's practice, head coach John Harbaugh was asked about the difficult decisions the Giants made as they put together their initial 53-man roste...
articles.body:
Head coach John Harbaugh explained some of the decisions made as the Giants cut down their 53-man roster...

Harbaugh hinted that Odell Beckham Jr. had done enough to crack the roster following Friday's preseason finale, and just two days later the team made the homecoming official.

Big Blue decided to keep the veteran heading into what will be his 13th NFL season.

"From beginning to end he earned it," Harbaugh said. "He looked like he was ready to help us -- you take the roster, you take the guys, you take the reps, the plays, what you need going into the season, and you pick the best guys.

"He was one of the best guys for us, he earned it, he earned his spot."

Beckham will be rotating in and out with different personnel groups, but he is expected to play a role in the receiver room heading into this season.

"Whatever it is that I need to provide, I'm looking to do that and more," the wideout said. "I've never shied away from competition or anything like that, so I feel like I can still produce and I know that's what I want to do."

One of the receivers who didn't make the cut in that crowded room was Braxton Berrios .

It didn't take long for Berrios to return to the organization after being cut free on Sunday, though, as he rejoined them on the practice squad on Monday.

Harbaugh said the plan is to treat him like he's playing on the 53 Man roster, for now.

"We have an opportunity, the way that you can work the roster now, to do that so that's the plan," he explained.

The Giants expect to have Berrios on their active roster ahead of the season opener, and he is currently penciled in to serve as their top punt returner.

There had been some buzz around the Giants potentially parting with Tyrone Tracy Jr. after his brutal preseason, but they ultimately elected to hold on to him.

They now head into the season with a bit of a crowded running back room compiled of returning starter Cam Skattebo , recently signed Najee Harris , Tracy, and veteran Devin Singletary .

"We just felt like they were part of our 53 best players, and it wasn't comfortable letting one of them go," Harbaugh said. "We felt all those guys would be able to play a role for us and we'd be able to have those guys contribute."

There's always some worry turning your special teams over to a rookie kicker, but the Giants aren't concerned at all.

Young Dominic Zvada was tremendous throughout camp and preseason action, beating out Ben Sauls for what's been a shaky spot for Big Blue over the past few seasons.

Zvada converted all three of his field goals during Friday's finale tune-up.

"He made a bunch of kicks before that, and I'm sure he'll make a bunch in the future," Harbaugh said. "And if Dominic misses one, it's not the end of the world, I learned that -- I think he's going to kick really well for us."

One of the players on the roster bubble the team decided to keep around is Nic Jones , with Art Green instead being waived with an injury settlement.

Jones is the sixth and final member of the CB room, but the team likes the versatility he brings.

"Art got nicked up, got the concussion, so that was part of it," Harbaugh said. "But Nic also plays nickel, he can play inside and outside, and he can play some safety -- we feel that he's a valuable piece for us."

Jones appeared in 13 games with the Giants last season, but logged just 20 defensive snaps.

articles.title: Colorado Rockies vs. Baltimore Orioles game discussion: Cade Povich vs. Tanner Gordon
articles.summary: Rockies need a win to snap their 9-game losing streak at Coors Field
articles.body:
After losing four games in a row, the Colorado Rockies (52-85) return to Coors Field for a six-game homestand starting with a showdown vs. the Baltimore Orioles (68-69) tonight.

The Rockies will then play the Cardinals to complete the homestand, which will be the second-to-last one in the 2026 season.

Tanner Gordon (1-4, 5.38 ERA) will be on the mound for Colorado. Gordon has gone back and forth from the bullpen and the starting rotation in 19 appearances this season since being called up on April 14. In seven starts, Gordon has a 1-3 record and 5.60 ERA.

His last two appearances have been starts, filling the rotation spot when the Rockies released Michael Lorenzen. After getting beat up by Cleveland on Aug. 21, when he gave up five runs on nine hits with two walks and two strikeouts in 5.1 innings, Gordon bounced back with a quality start against the Guardians when he held Washington to one run on six hits with no walks and five strikeouts in seven innings.

LHP Cade Povich (2-1, 4.45 ERA) will get the start for Baltimore. The 26-year-old third-round pick from the 2021 MLB Draft made his big league debut in June of 2024 and has yo-yoed between the Orioles and the farm system, along with juggling injuries, since. He's made six appearances this season for the Orioles and was just recalled earlier on Monday to make the start.

He had mixed results in August so far, throwing a six-inning shutout with seven strikeouts, one walk and seven hits against the Los Angeles Angels on Aug. 4 before Texas scored three runs on him in three innings with two walks and two strikeouts on Aug. 9. Monday will mark Povich's first appearance at Coors Field.

The Rockies have fared well in interleague play so far this season, going 16-17. However, the Orioles are coming off a three-game sweep of the A's.

It will be worth watching the weather as it's been cloudy in Denver and there's a chance of rain this evening.

When the project had been initially announced , Chase said he was doing the podcast with Bengals teammate Tee Higgins. It's unclear what happened between then and now.

Now, the "plus add-ons" is doing a lot of work here and there's a lot we don't know about what that means and how easily achievable they are. But considering Kevin Danso cost £21m a couple of years ago, £7m makes me reconsider this transfer… slightly. To be clear, I don't really rate Adarabioyo that much and don't think he's as good a defender as Danso — and Danso is our 4th/5th CB remember — but I can't really argue that much with the price. What I hope is that Tosin isn't priced to sell because Chelsea are that desperate to get rid of him because he flat out sucks, but I guess we're going to find that out pretty soon no matter what!

Do I still like this deal? No. Is it as bad a deal as I first thought? Also no. I'll have to hold those two things in tension for a while.

The Seattle Seahawks made the somewhat surprising decision to not just release veteran wide receiver Cody White, but to not even retain him on the practice squad like has been the norm over the past couple of seasons. We now know that the next chapter of White's career will be with his former Seahawks offensive coordinator.

White has signed with the Las Vegas Raiders practice squad, which will reunite him with new Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak.

The Raiders have scarcely looked at signing available former Seahawks players, but now they have Cody on the practice squad and free agent signing Dareke Young on their 53-man active roster. If you've taken a look at the Raiders' receiver depth chart, there is a more viable path to game day elevations if not an outright promotion to the active roster for Cody. White joins the waiver-claimed Jared Ivey as the first two Seahawks roster cuts confirmed to be heading elsewhere this season.

White was in competition with Ricky White III, Montorie Foster Jr, and Emmanuel Henderson Jr for the bottom-end of Seattle's wide receiver depth chart. With Jake Bobo out for the year, there figured to be a reasonable chance that Cody would either be on the active roster or signed back to Seattle's practice squad. The fact that neither happened is yet another strong endorsement for the rise of Foster, who appeared to separate himself pretty clearly from Ricky White and Henderson throughout camp and preseason.

We'll always have this moment, Cody White! And you've got a ring as a result.

articles.title: Rams 53-man roster: Does LA have enough tackles and defensive backs?
articles.summary: Nine OL and eight DB’s are a mirage. The Rams are dangerously thin at tackle and in the secondary.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams may boast one of the best rosters in professional football history on paper.

But margins are extremely thin in the NFL. For every position of strength—like the defensive line with Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald, and others—there is somewhere where LA is hoping people don't notice just how thin they are running .

I spy two places that are concerning and could grow even more so should attrition strike: offensive tackle and defensive back.

The Rams effectively turned in a roster with three tackles and almost no reserve secondary players. It's not a nitpick—it's a reality.

Alaric Jackson is still awaiting word from the league that he's in the clear. Until then, a suspension will linger over his head. David Quessenberry is the next man up at left tackle. That probably isn't good enough. Rookie Keagen Trost will miss at least the first four games of the season.

On the defensive side, the Rams have truly cut out all fat. There's nothing left at safety or corner.

Jaylen Watson and Trent McDuffie are entrenched as starters. McDuffie could play often in the slot, which means Rams fans will probably see more of Emmanuel Forbes on the outside than they realize. Josh Wallace also made the cut but hasn't played outside much over his tenure in Los Angeles.

At safety behind Kamren Curl, Kamren Kinchens, and Quentin Lake is only Jaylen McCollough. McCollough isn't really a backup—he's someone who carved out a decent role as a situational contributor a year ago.

Running skinny at these positions is a direct relationship to keeping seven receivers, five tight ends, and three quarterbacks. WR#7, TE#5, nor QB#3 are going to keep Matthew Stafford upright or help protect a lead into the playoffs. These are luxuries.

We've read this book before. 2022 brought intense attrition starting with the offensive line. Stafford shortly followed when the Rams couldn't block a soul. Before we knew it, half the roster was prematurely calling it a season.

Did the Rams not learn their lesson? A weakened secondary would make a great sequel, although it runs the risk of ending the same way.

Women's Intercontinental Championship Match: Sol Ruca vs. Raquel Rodriguez (c)

Backstage, Royce Keys and OTM attacked The Bloodline in the parking garage, leaving The Usos lying and bloodied.

Jacob Fatu made the save, chasing the newcomers off with a pipe and setting the stage for that new chapter of the saga to be a significant part of this week's show.

After Sol Ruca and Raquel Rodriguez made their way to the ring for their Women's Intercontinental Championship Match, Fatu appeared on the commentary table and vowed to "dog walk you three motherf*****s," which led to his microphone being cut.

The idea of Netflix blurring blood content on WWE TV when viewers can flip over and stream entries in the Saw franchise seems rather asinine.

This was a strong way to open the show, with an air of unpredictability, not to mention a group that can prove to be even more dangerous than the most dominant family in the sport.

Fatu is going to be the biggest, most unhinged babyface in the company by this time next year and if not, a creative shake-up will be warranted.

Women's Intercontinental Championship Match: Sol Ruca vs. Raquel Rodriguez

Last Time in Action: Sol Ruca defeated Lyra Valkyria (Raw, August 17); Raquel Rodriguez and Roxanne Perez lost to Iyo Sky and Sol Ruca (Raw, August 10)

Seeking to avenge her loss to Big Sexy and regain the Women's Intercontinental Championship, Ruca started her match with Rodriguez red-hot, taking the fight to the champion and wiping her out at ringside. She applied the tarantula, too, but Rodriguez halted her momentum with a cross-body block on the arena floor.

The heel dominated the action from there until Ruca mounted a comeback. She fended off Rodriguez and even thwarted interference from Liv Morgan and Roxanne Perez.

Unfortunately for her, Lyra Valkyria appeared, raked her eyes, and allowed Rodriguez to score the successful title defense with the Tejana Bomb.

The match itself was perfectly fine, if nothing more, but this was all about Valkyria's involvement and the escalation of her rivalry with Ruca. While this should move Ruca out of the IC title picture for the time being, expect a Triple Threat match to be announced sooner rather than later.

It was nice to see Ruca fired up and showing some intensity early on here. She has been so one-dimensional to this point in her main roster run that it would be nice to see her evolve her persona.

Last Time in Action: Chad Gable defeated Rey Mysterio (Raw, August 17)

Intercontinental champion Chad Gable hit the ring for a promo and credited the Mexican people for their role in his title reign. He said he planned to have a role on Raw's show in Mexico City and gave props to Dragon Lee.

That brought out the masked luchador, but before he could see much of anything, "All Ego" Ethan Page interrupted and staked his claim to a shot at the title. Gable said he has a list of guys who should have a title shot, but Page is nowhere near the top.

Lee and Page exchanged insults and Gable offered an IC title shot to the winner of a match right here, right now.

This was a formulaic segment designed to set up a match that could have been a backstage segment or a pre-taped segment. With that said, it was nice to see these three guys get mic time on Monday night, as opposed to the normal handful of Superstars allowed that time.

The idea of Gable vs. Lee in Mexico is mighty appealing and something the latter has earned based on his in-ring performances of late.

Page feels like he has taken a significant step back creatively in recent months and that is a shame for a guy with potential to be a top heel on this show.

Last Time in Action: Dragon Lee lost to Rey Fenix (Raw, August 24); Ethan Page lost to Je'Von Evans (Raw, August 3)

With a championship opportunity against Gable at stake, Lee and Page battled in a competitive match that escalated with a dive that sent All Ego across the commentary table at ringside.

Lee tried for a second dive, but Page caught him in the face, stunning him. He sent him into an exposed turnbuckle and looked to have the match won, but the referee noticed it and refused to count.

The luchador recovered and delivered Enter the Dragon for the win.

This was a solid match that got a little too cute late when it really could have been a clean win for Lee. Still, the right guy went over to set up a big match with Gable in Mexico, a match that will have all of the potential in the world to steal the show.

WWE loves that exposed turnbuckle spot right now. This was not the first time we have seen it in recent weeks.

A big win for Lee. He has the potential to be the type of Superstar who can build momentum and get over on his abilities alone.

Last Time in Action: Roman Reigns defeated Seth Rollins (SummerSlam, August 2)

The OTC took to the squared circle to address the WWE Universe and what he perceives as a lack of respect from the likes of Solo Sikoa and LA Knight.

Before he could go any further, the latter interrupted him, staring the World Heavyweight Champion down from the top of the ramp.

Knight accused Reigns of recycling material from three years ago and said he thought the Tribal Chief was better than that. "I've been calling your name for months, and all you have done is put your family and tournaments that you know I can't enter between us."

The Megastar joined Reigns in the center of the ring. Before anything physical could occur, cameras caught a bloodied Solo Sikoa backstage, with producers and officials checking on him.

Knight left the ring to check on him but caught a cheap shot from Reigns.

Unfortunately, this did feel exactly like Knight referred to it as: recycled. It felt like plenty of segments we have seen before, with the Sikoa attack sprinkled in to keep it relevant to the overarching story.

Knight is on fire right now and is clearly feeling himself in this latest flirtation with the main event. As he should.

Je'Von Evans vs. Dominik Mysterio; Evans and Joe Hendry vs. Mysterio and JD McDonagh

Last Time in Action: Je'Von Evans lost to Big Cass (Raw, August 24) ; Dominik Mysterio lost to Dragon Lee (Raw, August 10)

The match between Evans and Mysterio was short-lived as interference from JD McDonagh, just as the babyface was gaining momentum, resulted in a disqualification.

As the heels beat down Evans, Joe Hendry's music played, and the former NXT champion hit the ring to make the save. Infuriated by the chaos that had reigned supreme tonight, general manager Adam Pearce appeared and ordered a tag team match.

Hendry received a hot tag and fired up on his opponents, taking the fight to them and even flying through the air to wipe The Judgment Day out at ringside.

Unfortunately for the Scottish-born competitor, his momentum would not last as McDonagh downed him with a headbutt and Mysterio pinned him to pick up the win.

A perfectly solid match that did nothing of note to further any ongoing stories and if anything, was detrimental to Evans, who is still reeling from his loss to Big Cass last week.

Evans defeated Mysterio via disqualification;

The "singles match turns into a tag team match" is a lazy booking choice of a bygone era. It felt like microcosm of this show, for the most part.

Don't look now, but Mysterio actually won a match in this back half of 2026.

Backstage, Becky Lynch and Stephanie Vaquer engaged in a tense exchange. For the love of all that is good, can we just get this match in all of its glory already?

Paul Heyman Previews Oba Femi vs. Bron Breakker

A video package hyped the match-up between Oba Femi and Bron Breakker on Sunday Night's Main Event, airing live on Peacock this weekend, before Cathy Kelley caught up with Paul Heyman backstage.

The Wise Man said that the match is being billed as "for the future of WWE," which begs the question: what becomes of the loser of that match?

Still one of the best talkers in the industry, he did as much to put over the implications of the match as anything the creative team had to that point.

Rather than selling it based on two big, bad, young stars of the future, he sold the emotional impact it could have on the man who comes up short. A great promo.

Quite literally everything would be better with Heyman providing his viewpoint on it.

World Heavyweight Championship No. 1 Contender's Tournament Final: Penta vs. Rey Fenix

Last Time in Action: Penta, Rey Fenix, and Dragon Lee defeated Los Perros del Mal (AAA Ola de Calor, August 30)

The Lucha Brothers exploded in the main event of Monday's show as Penta and Fenix squared off for the chance to challenge Roman Reigns for the World Heavyweight Championship on September 14 in Mexico City.

A high-energy battle saw the elder sibling control the bout early and often, but a moonsault press by Fenix brought the AAA Cruiserweight Champion back into the match.

Penta attempted a sunset flip powerbomb, but Fenix landed on his feet. He further stunned his brother by kicking out of the Penta Driver at two.

Frustrated, Penta drove Fenix through the announce table, but was still unable to put him down for three. He added the Sacrifice, seemingly dislocating Fenix's arm. When the younger competitor urged him to put him down, Penta charged at him and nearly lost via hurricanrana.

Penta recovered and delivered the Mexican Destroyer for the win.

After the match, Reigns joined Penta in the ring and came face-to-face with the babyface, raising his title high overhead and being met with the "cero miedo" from his new No. 1 contender.

Sure, this felt rather subdued compared to other matches between the two but it was still excellent and had fans in Cleveland hanging on every spot. The pacing was great, escalating until the action-packed finale.

The right guy went over, but this entire tournament was a wake-up call for the rest of WWE to stop sleeping on Fenix.

This was a one-match show for the most part, and that match did not disappoint. Penta and Fenix tore the house down in the marquee match of the night, highlighting their immense talent and proving why they were the right two to compete for the title opportunity.

The main event elevated this one significantly. It was that good. The rest of the show, outside of the phenomenal Jacob Fatu promo, was rather lethargic and did little to drum up excitement for Sunday's Main Event.

It was a show that existed for the sake of it, with strong follow-up from Keys and OTM, but nothing much else.

articles.title: Texas Tech head coach blasts USC, Lincoln Riley, for poor attendance at LA Coliseum in Week Zero
articles.summary: Joey Maguire said Texas Tech fans are tough enough to show up in the heat, taking a not-so-subtle shot at USC's sparse LA Coliseum attendance.
articles.body: Boy oh boy, do we need a full slate of college football games to start. Immediately, if not sooner. Despite the LSU Tigers program under Lane Kiffin essentially blowing up the college football model by adding NFL players in order to make their team better and pivotal week one storylines to track, the only topic of discussion around the sport this week has been the attendance at USC's home opener. The Trojans hosted San Jose State at the LA Coliseum on Saturday at noon, a game time that made little sense for everyone other than NBC. SC entered the game as 38-point favorites, temperatures were in the mid-90's with extreme, and unusual, humidity for Southern California, and the kickoff time ensured there'd be no shade or relief from the miserable conditions. USC FOOTBALL RIPPED FOR PATHETIC CROWD AT HOME OPENER: 'ABSOLUTELY EMBARRASSING' Unsurprisingly, many chose to stay home, rationally deciding that they could simply wait for the weather and a more favorable kickoff time to deal with the atrocious LA traffic, elevated parking prices, long walk, and terrible security lines. This has sparked days of outrage and clickbait videos from commentators and analysts in comfortable studios who are certain they'd sit in the heat to watch a full game that was over within 15 minutes. All while ignoring the many examples of other big schools, like the Florida Gators, that have struggled to fill seats for noon games in August. Now we can add the head coach of the Texas Tech Red Raiders, a program known for its moral character, to the list of complainants. At a news conference on Monday, Joey Maguire explained, just before taking a shot, that he did not want to "take any shots," before saying he's excited to play in front of a sold out crowd in Lubbock this weekend. "Not to take any shots because I have a lot of respect for USC and Lincoln Riley, but man, it's really awesome to be playing in Lubbock, Texas, knowing we're going to be playing front of 60,000, and it's going to be warm," he said. "It's going to be every bit as warm as it was Saturday. The great thing is we got some really tough people in West Texas that love their football and they're going to show up." DOES USC'S POOR OPENING GAME ATTENDANCE MEAN LINCOLN RILEY'S ON THE HOT SEAT ALREADY? It actually won't be as warm in Lubbock as it was in LA, with a forecast high of 92 degrees and lower humidity. And the game is at 4 p.m., meaning the sun will be going down behind the stadium by the second half, instead of only getting increasingly hot as the game wears on. OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Though, since weather is the topic of conversation in college football right now, it is a credit to fans in Lubbock that they show up to watch their teams in the heat. The problem though? They have no choice. Most Texas Tech home games in August and September are going to be miserable, because the weather in Lubbock in August and September is miserable. There's no, "I'll just go to the next game because it'll be more comfortable," because doing so would mean missing half the season. Same with Gainesville, Florida, and most of the South. The weather is objectively awful for two straight months, which means you have little choice but to subject yourself to hell in order to watch the team play. With USC, by contrast, these outlier heatwaves are pretty easily avoidable. The forecast for Friday night's game against Fresno State, for example, is 72 degrees. By the end of the game, it'll be 68. Some fans make the rational decision to simply...go to that game instead, not waste their time to watch 15 minutes of competitive football. Especially when there are multiple events per week that compete for entertainment dollars. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM Fans in other parts of the country have no choice and are used to atrocious conditions, because they live in places with atrocious summer climates. There's no competition for Texas Tech football in Lubbock, not the NFL, not Major League Baseball, and not Major League Soccer, all of which will have games in LA in the coming weeks. Should USC's attendance have been higher? Yeah, absolutely. Did it fill in more after kickoff? Also yes, though obviously well below what it could have been. For those who've never been to the Coliseum, it's in downtown LA, which means horrific traffic trying to get to the USC campus. There's little parking at the Coliseum, meaning fans are forced into a nightmarish hellscape of distant structures, and the security lines are infamously awful at an old stadium. Late arriving crowds are part of the LA sports experience, even at USC, because getting places in LA is an unpredictable guessing game. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! Oh, and not that it matters to Maguire or to anyone else, for that matter, but there are plenty of good seats available for most Texas Tech home games this year. Yes, week one is sold out, but their game against Arizona has thousands of tickets just waiting for those "tough" fans to snap up. Even their "biggest" home game, against Arizona State, has seats readily available. Lower level tickets are $170, whereas desirable seats for SC's home game against Oregon in September are $425-$475. For a family of four, that's nearly $2,000 to go to a game, with parking and stadium concessions. Maybe that's part of the problem too, USC's administration simply pricing their tickets too high for what the market can support. Particularly given the competition in LA and Southern California. USC's student composition has also changed dramatically in recent decades, as the school now has a shockingly high percentage of international students, thanks to their wealthy donor parents, who have little interest in football. But nuance, rationality, perspective, and experience are not valuable commodities in college football, however, considering social media dunks are far more exciting and attention grabbing.

articles.title: Yankees stoop to Angels’ level, suffer blowout loss in Anaheim
articles.summary: The Yankees beat themselves in a series opener to forget.
articles.body:
The Yankees seemed to be a team that could do no wrong on Sunday when they sent the Red Sox home with a 16-1 thumping that left many among their commentariat more than a little salty. That's a heck of a win to build some momentum on as the final full month of the regular season awaits. Better yet, they got to fly out to Orange County to take on the lowly Angels, riding a seven-game losing streak and playing obligatory, meaningless ball.

But momentum is a fickle thing. Just because a team can catch fire after a great game doesn't mean they will. It doesn't shield them from a ridiculously poor performance the following night. That was perhaps a nice way of putting the Yankees' effort in the series opener. Elmer Rodríguez plunked two batters with two outs before allowing both runners to score, José Caballero committed a pair of ugly errors in the field, and the offense checked out early in a 10-1 loss best placed in a filing cabinet in a dingy basement somewhere. The Bombers lost a game to the Red Sox in the Wild Card race, and remain 4.5 games back of the Rays in the AL East.

Rodríguez encountered his first bit of adversity in the third inning, allowing a leadoff double to ninth-place hitter Tyler Heineman. Heineman had allowed two Yankees to advance into scoring position back in the first when he lost track of a ball in the dirt. His starter Walbert Ureña worked around it, and the double made up for the mistake. But Rodríguez appeared well on the way to working around that double until he issued a two-out walk to Wade Meckler to extend the rally. Vaughn Grissom followed with a jam shot to center which found plenty of room in front of Trent Grisham, allowing Heineman to score for a 1-0 Angels lead.

An inning later, Elmer re-established himself by grabbing a pair of routine outs, including his fifth strikeout of the night against Josh Lowe. Then, he plunked consecutive batters on runaway curveballs to bring up the top of the order for the third time and get the bullpen to warm up behind him. Zach Neto had gotten his ticket punched each of his first two times up against Rodríguez, but the third time was the charm as he punched a single through the left side to bring another costly two-out run home.

The Bombers tried to grab the final out at third, but were unsuccessful, and Neto was able to slink to second in the meantime, giving Mike Trout an opportunity with two runners in scoring position. Now fully untethered from any semblance of command he had shown in the first three innings, he let a fastball leak over the inner half; all Trout had to do was flip it around. Two runs scored on his base hit, the Angels suddenly led 4-0, and Elmer was out of the game.

Hitting consecutive batters with two outs is a particularly exasperating unforced error. It's particularly strange that the curveball, a pitch he seemed to have on a string early in the evening, was the culprit both times. He churned out two absolute jalopies off the assembly line in quick succession. That those dud curves happened to strike the eighth- and ninth-place hitters only made it more inexcusable, since it gave RBI chances to two of the only guys in the Angels lineup who can reliably cash in on those mistakes.

Ureña, on the other hand, took the missed Yankee opportunity at the top of the show and ran with it, retiring 11 consecutive batters after that little wild pitch. I'm sure the Yankees had watched plenty of film on the 22-year-old righty, but facing his tricky pitch mix capped off by a dastardly changeup that misses barrels and keeps balls in the yard. Ureña used his mix to clip the Yankees' wings for half the night, until a rocket from Spencer Jones got the Yankees out of containment and on the board.

Jones' eighth homer of the year was an impressive clout, but it was just a solo shot, and didn't give the Bombers any additional kindling to roar back to life. The Halos promptly responded with a leadoff chalk-hugging double from Grissom and a sinking line drive from Christian Moore that Jones, even with his long strides, couldn't make up enough ground to grab. In a flash, the solo homer was nullified.

But this loss felt just a little too dignified. We needed a true circus play to expunge all the good vibes that might have accompanied Sunday's evisceration of the Red Sox.

Fulmer tried to pick the speedy Moore off at second base. Caballero appeared to be looking elsewhere as the ball clonked off his glove and into center field. Moore aggressively cut the bag at third and dashed for home the wishes of his base coach, daring a defense caught on its heels to make a play.

The thing about the Yankees is those kinds of dares tend to work without any trouble. This gamble from Moore was anything but. Trent Grisham's throw in from center had no juice or true direction on it, so Luis Garcia Jr. dashed over from first in an attempt to relay it home. He threw the ball roughly 15 feet wide of home. I wish I could say that sequence surprised me, but I'm not exactly new here.

Luis Gil entering in the sixth inning to make his first MLB appearance since April 26th only served to give this contest an even more ersatz quality. Gil did his job and appeared to induce a routine double-play ball to shortstop, which would have ended the inning. But Caballero had not done anything good in the field tonight, and he wasn't about to start here. He booted the grounder, then rushed a low throw to first that Garcia failed to scoop. Inning-ending double play? Try no outs and another run scored.

I remind you this team shoved their biggest rival—and closest peer in the Wild Card race—into a locker yesterday. But those sorts of rousing victories in the past have never stopped them from pulling this kind of malarkey shortly afterward. Such was again the case here.

Jones' home run in the fifth marked Ureña's only blip as he continued his splendid rookie campaign with seven strong innings. The Yankees appeared as desperate to get this game over with as the poor saps who had stayed up to watch them. The Angels understandably wanted to make this moment last, so they grabbed three runs off David Bednar in the eighth to put themselves in double figures. Truly awful stuff from everyone involved.

Good news came in before first pitch tonight, as the Mets eked out a 3-2 victory over the Rays in St. Petersburg. Even as the Mariners blew a late lead against the Red Sox and let them escape with a win in the 10th, the Yankees still had a great chance to gain ground in the divisional battle. Shockingly, they refused to take advantage of the opportunity, losing a laugher to one of the worst teams in baseball; a team playing out the string on an utterly lost decade, dead in the water. The Yankees played necromancers tonight.

At least it's Gerrit Cole bump night tomorrow. The Orange County native and UCLA Athletic Hall of Famer will take the hill at The Big A against a major what-if guy: Grayson Rodriguez. First pitch is once again due for the refreshingly honest time of 9:38pm ET on YES.

articles.title: Report: No. 23 Prospect in Baseball, Ethan Salas, Gets the Call
articles.summary: It's official. The San Diego Padres' No. 1 prospect, Ethan Salas, has been called up to the big leagues, per Kevin Acee of the San Diego Union-Tribune. He wi...
articles.body:
It's official. The San Diego Padres' No. 1 prospect, Ethan Salas , has been called up to the big leagues, per Kevin Acee of the San Diego Union-Tribune . He will join the team in Cincinnati for the last two games of their series against the Reds before returning to Petco Park with the club for the upcoming homestand. It's a massive development for the Friars with the roster expanding from 26 to 28 players on September 1.

Yet it's not all that surprising. Plenty of analysts around the league, including this writer, believed that Salas would be called up once the rosters expanded in the stretch run. There's no downside to it, and it gives the young catcher an opportunity to get his feet wet in the big leagues. It's a fantastic move for San Diego, and it offers the 20-year-old prospect time to develop versus big-league pitching.

Report: Ethan Salas To Be Called Up by Padres

Even if the rosters weren't expanding, Salas would still have earned a spot on the roster. In 72 games in Double-A, Salas hit .286/.361/.417 with 108 total bases. He hit seven homers and swiped 14 bags in that time, showcasing some ridiculous power/speed combination despite the fact that Salas is a catcher.

Since being called up to the El Paso Chihuahuas (the Padres' Triple-A affiliate), Salas has slashed a ridiculous .326/.410/.539 with a .949 OPS and three home runs. Those numbers are certainly somewhat inflated by the fact that Salas plays in the Pacific Coast League. The PCL is well-known for its hitter-friendly environs, but Salas has still managed to play above even those loftier standards.

This is massive news for San Diego. Salas has been one of their most tantalizing prospects for years. Despite regressing due to injuries in 2025, he's stormed back into the conversation, becoming the No. 23 prospect in all of baseball. Salas represents a bright future for a Padres core that includes superstar veterans and incredibly talented young players alike.

At the end of the day, Salas isn't playing for a spot on the postseason roster. It would be awesome if he rakes during his time at the big-league level, but that likely wouldn't change much. Salas is a young player with his whole future ahead of him. Calling him up now won't jeopardize that, but it could if the Friars don't handle it correctly. They need to give Salas time to develop without the pressure of performing right away. Too many great prospects have flamed out quickly due to that kind of stress. Hopefully, Salas won't.
